_comment: The pack's progression route, source for the FTB Quests book. tools/quests/build.py turns it into config/ftbquests/quests/ and checks it against the progression checker. Each quest: key (unique), title, subtitle, desc (lines), item (an item task, detected automatically) or checkmark: true (the player ticks it), deps (quest keys, any chapter), big (drawn larger), optional, extra_items (more item tasks). Fuller tasks go in tasks: {item, count}, {filter (an FTB Filter System expression), any (its items/tags, for the checker), count}, {type: checkmark|observation|kill|dimension|biome, ...}, optional per task. Also per quest: icon, size, shape, dependency_requirement (e.g. one_completed), hide_dependency_lines, unchecked (the checker can't reach its items; don't count that as a problem), pos (x, y; used when the chapter has layout: manual), source (where ported text came from). Chapters: key, title, icon, group (a key in groups), layout (manual: use each quest's pos; otherwise laid out from dependencies). Quests from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0) were ported with tools/quests/port_tfg.py.
title: The Route

quests.title: The Route
quests.subtitle: TFC, then Create, then GregTech
desc: TerraFirmaCraft on a real-scale Earth, mechanized with Create, industrialized with GregTech, with airships from Create Aeronautics.
The route: TFC's stone, copper and bronze ages; Create from the bronze age; TFC's iron; GregTech's steam age, which runs on Create parts; TFC steel; GregTech electricity. Airships open with brass.
Look up any recipe in EMI: hover an item and press R for its recipes, U for its uses. TFC's field guide explains survival, knapping, pottery and metalworking.
On a server, /startat <latitude> <longitude> moves you once to any place on Earth (south and west are negative), e.g. /startat 59.33 18.07 for Stockholm.

quests.title: Stone Tools
quests.subtitle: Knap loose rocks
desc: Pick up loose rocks and sticks from the ground. Knap rocks into tool heads (use two rocks), then craft a head with a stick. A knife and an axe come first: the axe fells whole trees, the knife cuts straw from grass and plants.
You've officially entered the Stone Age! Stone tools are enough for basic survival, but eventually you'll want metal tools for much better speed, durability and tool options.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Fire
quests.subtitle: A firepit
desc: Craft a Firestarter from two sticks. Throw one log and three sticks on the ground (up to five pieces of kindling, such as straw, raise the odds), then hold right-click on them with the firestarter until they catch.

The firepit cooks food, heats metal and later lights pit kilns and charcoal pits. Heating sticks in it makes torches. Keep it burning by adding logs (or stick bundles or peat) in its screen; if it goes out, add fuel and light it again.
Monsters don't spawn on the surface here, but nocturnal predators prowl at night.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Pottery
quests.subtitle: A fired small vessel
desc: Knap clay into a small vessel and ingot molds, then fire them in a pit kiln (straw and logs over the pottery, lit).

The vessel holds up to four items like a small bag (food inside keeps longer), but more importantly it's your first tool for working with metals: fill it with ore, fire it in a pit kiln to &lmelt&r the metal, then use it to pour into a mold. Its tooltip tells you what the ores inside will melt into, which is especially useful for alloys.
Alloys need specific percentages of each metal. Copper is great right away, but you could make your very first metal tools from bronze instead.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Charcoal
quests.subtitle: Fuel that burns hot
desc: Stack logs in a pit, cover them and light them: a charcoal pit. Charcoal is hot enough for a forge, the bloomery and the blast furnace, and you'll need a lot of it.

Sneak and right-click with logs to place log piles in your pit; the more logs in the piles, the more charcoal. Cover them with non-flammable blocks, leaving one pile open, light it with a firestarter or a torch, then cover it too. Once the smoke stops, dig out the charcoal piles, preferably with a shovel.
Later, with wrought iron plates, GregTech's coke oven turns logs into charcoal (plus creosote) and coal into coke.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Copper
quests.subtitle: Your first metal
desc: Melt native copper, malachite or tetrahedrite in a small vessel and pour it into a fired ingot mold. Ingot molds have a 10% chance to break each cast.
TFC ores come in grades: small 10 mB, poor 15, normal 25, rich 35; an ingot is 100 mB.
Anvils aren't cheap! Each anvil takes 14 ingots, welded into 7 double ingots: 140 small ore pieces' worth of copper. You might want to start mining (or panning) at this point if you haven't already.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Copper Anvil
quests.subtitle: Metalworking
desc: Weld ingots into double ingots and shape them on a stone anvil. The anvil makes tools, sheets and most metal parts.

From here you climb the anvil tiers: copper (I); bronze, bismuth bronze and black bronze (II); wrought iron (III); steel (IV); black steel (V); red and blue steel (VI). An anvil works metals of its own tier and welds metals one tier higher, so each new anvil opens new tools and parts.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Find some Rocks
quests.subtitle: Grug smash rock
desc:
As you begin your journey, the first thing you'll notice is a completely changed world. You can no longer break trees with your fists, but fret not, for any caveman is not a real caveman without his stone tools!

Instead of crafting a wooden pickaxe, you can just pick up rocks from the ground. Begin by collecting at least 4 rocks. You can collect rocks by breaking or right-clicking them with an empty hand. Obsidian shards knap just like rocks.
{@pagebreak}
{image:tfc:textures/gui/book/gui/rock_knapping.png width:100 height:100 align:center fit:true}
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Thirsty?
quests.subtitle: Remember to drink water!
desc:
Thirst is the blue bar by your hunger bar. You can and will die of dehydration if you don't keep it filled! The easiest way to have a drink is from fresh water in the wild: right-click a lake or river with an empty hand.

Tick this off once you've had a drink of fresh water. You don't have to worry about purifying water here, though Salt Water will just make you more thirsty.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Find some Sticks
quests.subtitle: You gotta handle that tool somehow
desc:
Another abundant item on the ground are sticks, which have many uses! They can create tools, torches, firestarters and more. Breaking leaves by hand drops sticks too.

To avoid having your inventory get clogged with different types of twigs, you can craft them into 'regular' sticks to stack them together. Later, at a workbench, nine sticks make a Stick Bunch and two bunches a Stick Bundle, which burns like a log in firepits, pit kilns and charcoal pits.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Knapping
quests.subtitle: Just like the olden days of the Paleolithic
desc:
Rocks can be "Knapped", which is the process of shaping a basic material into a usable form by smacking them together. Rock Knapping requires at least two rocks: hold them and right-click the air to open the Knapping interface. You can then "chip off" pieces of your rock to create a stone tool head. All the shapes for different tools can be found in EMI and the Field Guide.

The two most important tools for the beginning of your journey are a Stone Knife and a Stone Axe, so try knapping those tool heads.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Primitive Tools
quests.subtitle: Turns out hitting stones together is quite useful
desc: While stone and obsidian are relatively simple and primitive materials, they're what you're stuck with until you learn how to work with metals. Some other useful tools include the Javelin, which can be thrown like a vanilla Trident, the Hammer, which you'll need for flux and anvils, and the Hoe, which allows you to farm.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Gather Logs
quests.subtitle: Timber!
desc:
With your new Stone Axe, you'll be able to chop down trees. Breaking the base of a tree fells the whole tree, logs and leaves included; break leaves one by one if you want saplings and sticks.

Gather at least 10 logs -- 8 of these will be used for a Pit Kiln while the other two will be used for a Fire Pit.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Gather Straw
quests.subtitle: You can also use a Hoe if you want
desc:
Most grasses you find in the overworld can be harvested for Straw when broken with a Knife or Hoe. Straw has a number of uses for crafting, but you'll want at least 8 to create a Pit Kiln.

Straw can also be crafted into Thatch, a simple building block that players and mobs pass right through, and two thatch blocks make a Thatch Bed.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Hungry?
quests.subtitle: Where's my easy food?
desc:
In TerraFirmaCraft, the world is a harsh place, and one of the most important aspects of survival is being able to obtain food. Most food by itself yields little nutritional value, and all of it rots in time.

Begin by obtaining any form of food.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Basic Cooking
quests.subtitle: You don't want to die from eating raw meat, do you?
desc:
Cooking raw meat is an important step for getting protein: cooked meat keeps much longer than raw meat.

The simplest way to cook meat is in a Fire Pit (see the Fire quest): put it in the firepit's heating slot.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Soups
quests.subtitle: Which store were you in?
desc:
By crafting a pot and some bowls out of clay, you'll be able to create soups! Put the fired pot on a lit firepit, fill it with water, add 3 to 5 fruits, vegetables or meats and let it boil, then scoop the soup out with a bowl.

Soups are one of the first and easiest ways to create more complex meals. Unlike eating plain ingredients, they let you consume multiple nutrients at once!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Mechanic: Nutrition
quests.subtitle: What do you mean I can't just eat steak?
desc:
Each basic food contains nutrients, split into 5 categories: &lGrain&r, &lFruit&r, &lVegetables&r, &lProtein&r and &lDairy&r.

While you could eat only one kind of nutrient such as Protein, your maximum health will suffer, while a balanced diet gives you much higher max health. Only recent meals count, so keep eating a variety; soups, salads and sandwiches combine several nutrients at once.

Look at the field guide's "Food and Water" section for full details. The nutrition tab of your inventory shows your current levels.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Meals
quests.subtitle: GET IN MAH BELLEH!
desc: These are just some of the basic meals you can create. Soups, salads, and sandwiches are your go-tos for easy high saturation combined meals.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Mechanic: Hydration
quests.subtitle: Yet another bar to keep full...
desc:
Water is an important resource, not just for staying hydrated! Setting up a base near a fresh lake or river is recommended, so you have easy access to the stuff. Other items can quench your thirst, such as certain types of food or drinks.

Water won't always be available when you go exploring, however, so here are some ways to carry drinks around with you. Drinking consumes 100mB from the container.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Ceramic Jug
quests.subtitle: Relatively easy water
desc:
Knap a Jug out of clay and fire it in a Pit Kiln. A Ceramic Jug is the earliest liquid container you can craft, but it only holds 100 mB, so you'll need to refill it after every drink: right-click water with it, then hold right-click to drink.

The Jug is relatively fragile and has a small chance to break when you drink from it! You can also blow into it to make it whistle.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Wooden Bucket
quests.subtitle: Not as easy as you think
desc:
Carrying around a water source would be an easy way to never run out, but it doesn't work here.

A Wooden Bucket, made from lumber, holds 1000 mB of any fluid for filling barrels and pots, but it cannot place source blocks: pouring it out only makes a small puddle that quickly disappears.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Weather
quests.subtitle: The weather for today? Pain.
desc:
A new world starts in early summer (June), with each month lasting 8 days. Seasons will change, and with them the temperature and rainfall, which affect crops, fruit trees, bushes and whether snow and ice form.

The Calendar and Climate tabs of your inventory show the date, the season, and your location's average and current temperature and rainfall. This world is a real-scale Earth, so its climate is the climate of the real place you're standing in: pick your farm site accordingly.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Clay Sources
quests.subtitle: You'll need a lot of this
desc:
Clay is an essential part of stone age tech! Similar to knapping rocks, clay can be molded into different shapes and then fired in a Pit Kiln to create a wide variety of items. Stone Tools and Clay Ceramics will be the backbone of your survival until you learn how to work with Metals.

Clay is found in patches in the ground, usually covered by grass, in areas with at least 175 mm of annual rainfall. Certain plants, known as "Clay Indicators" (athyrium fern, canna, goldenrod, pampas grass, perovskia and water canna), grow right on top of it. Smaller deposits sit close to rivers, lakes and ponds.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Clay
quests.subtitle: It's Clay!
desc: Gather some Clay: knapping takes 5 clay per item, and you'll want a vessel, a saw blade mold, ingot molds and more (see the next quests). Once you mold the clay, put the pieces in a Pit Kiln to bake them into Ceramic. You mold clay the same way you knap stone, but if you make a mistake you can just close the interface and reshape it.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Pit Kiln
quests.subtitle: Things are heating up now
desc:
The Pit Kiln is an early game method of heating items up. We'll use it to both fire our clay items, and most importantly, melt very basic ores and create our first metal tool, a Saw.

To create a pit kiln you'll need eight pieces of Straw, eight logs, something you want to heat up, and a Firestarter. Read the Field Guide's Pit Kilns section on how to create it - it's not the same as a Fire Pit!
{@pagebreak}
{image:tfc:textures/gui/book/tutorial/pit_kiln_2.png width:100 height:100 align:center}
{@pagebreak}
{image:tfc:textures/gui/book/tutorial/pit_kiln_3.png width:100 height:100 align:center}
{@pagebreak}
{image:tfc:textures/gui/book/tutorial/pit_kiln_4.png width:100 height:100 align:center}
{@pagebreak}
{image:tfc:textures/gui/book/tutorial/pit_kiln_5.png width:100 height:100 align:center}
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Saw Mold
quests.subtitle: Time for your first metal tool
desc: The first mold you should make out of clay is the Saw Mold. With it and some small amount of metal you can create a Saw. The Saw is an important tool, as it's required to create &lLumber&r, and with it, you'll be able to create your first &l&oWorkbench.&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Clay Products
quests.subtitle: I told you Clay was versatile.
desc: These are all the products you can make out of Clay. The Molds are used for metal working, the Vessels are used to hold items, and the others have uses explained in the Field Guide. Think you can knap them all?
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Pebbles with ore?
quests.subtitle: Your first metal is already available if you look for it.
desc:
Ore veins generate differently than what you might be used to - you can't just wander into a random cave. Instead, look for small pieces of ore lying on the surface among the loose rocks and sticks.

Can't find anything that melts into Copper (native copper, malachite or tetrahedrite)? Try looking in another rock type -- different ores spawn in different rocks. The field guide's ores section tells you where each one is found.
{@pagebreak}

These small pieces are indicators: a larger vein of the same ore lies somewhere nearby, probably underground and close to the surface. You don't have a pickaxe yet, so take note of the place where you found the ore! It'll be very useful later on.

Each piece is worth 10 mB of metal (an ingot is 100 mB), so collect as many as you can, but make sure you make a note of where you found them!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Metallic Saw
quests.subtitle: Time for your first metal tool
desc:
To begin making your Saw, put at least 100 mB of ore of your desired metal in a Vessel (ten small ore pieces). Afterwards, place the Vessel in a Pit Kiln and light it on fire.

Once the Pit Kiln burns out, take your vessel while the metal is still molten and use it to open the Casting interface. Simply place the fired Saw Blade Mold in its slot and watch it fill with your very first Saw Blade. Afterwards, combine your Saw Blade with a Stick and you'll create your Saw!
{@pagebreak}

While the easiest metal to work with is Copper, you can try your hand at the process of alloying. This quest accepts a saw of Copper or any of the three bronzes.

&lBismuth Bronze&r: Copper (50-65%), Zinc (20-30%) and Bismuth (10-20%).

&lBronze&r: Copper (88-92%) and Tin (8-12%). The most average of the bronzes.

&lBlack Bronze&r: Copper (50-70%), Silver (10-25%) and Gold (10-25%). Considerably more expensive.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Time for the Workbench
quests.subtitle: 3x3 crafting is within your grasp
desc:
Combine your new Saw with a Log in your crafting grid to create Lumber. 4 Lumber can then be crafted into Planks...

 and once you have 4 planks, its time to make your very first Workbench.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Workbench
quests.subtitle: This... is a Crafting Table
desc:
Congratulations! With your Workbench you've officially entered the Peak of the Stone Age. With it you'll be able to craft a multitude of new things with the items you've gathered so far. In this pack TFC workbenches also count as crafting tables wherever a recipe asks for one.

Now comes your main goal of the Primitive Age: proper metalworking with the Copper Anvil.

Sidenote: While you could gather enough materials to make 14 ingots of bronze right now, you won't be able to turn them into a bronze anvil without crafting the copper one first, sorry! At least anvils are recyclable: an anvil melts back into all 14 ingots' worth of metal.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Early Storage Options
quests.subtitle: Time to stop carrying all your junk in vessels
desc:
In the early game, you have a few simple storage options:

&lChest&r: Chests are cheap and easy to craft from lumber and have 18 slots. They hold items up to Large in size; Very Large items such as logs don't fit.

&lCrate&r: A Crate stores a single kind of item, but up to 36 stacks of it.

&lLarge Vessels&r: The cheapest to craft, only requiring clay, with nine slots. Sealed, they're ideal for food preservation. Available in a wide variety of colors too!

Baskets, shelves and tool racks round things out (see the field guide's Storage page). Keep food in sealed vessels: food left in chests can attract rats.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Barrels
quests.subtitle: Stephano?
desc:
Unlike their vanilla counterparts, Barrels here are used as Liquid Storage. Barrels are capable of storing a total of 10 Buckets of fluid, allowing for relatively simple storage of fluids.

You can also combine these fluids with other items, to create things like Leather, Glue, Mortar and more.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Barrel Rack
quests.subtitle: Now that's a nice rack!
desc:
The barrel rack can be used to stack barrels on top of each other, allowing you to be more space-efficient!

Consult your field guide for more specific information on how to use them.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Leather
quests.subtitle: Because of course everything has to be more complicated
desc:
When killed, wild animals drop raw hides. Hide cannot be used as leather directly and instead must be worked and processed first: soak it in limewater, scrape it on a log with a knife, soak it in water, then seal it in a barrel of tannin. The field guide's Leather Making page walks you through it.

Leather, just like Clay and Stone, can be Knapped, into Leather Armor, saddles and horse armor. In this pack Create's belts take leather (or burlap) too.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Leather Armor
quests.subtitle: Very basic protection
desc: Leather Armor, just like its Minecraft counterpart, is a very basic set of armor, knapped from leather. It doesn't last long, but a full suit gives decent protection against the predators of the early game.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Thatch Bed
quests.subtitle: A place to rest... somewhat
desc:
Utilizing some &bThatch&r and a &aLarge Raw Hide&r, you can create a &dThatch Bed.&r It cannot be used to sleep in, but it'll &cset your spawn point.&r

To create a Thatch Bed, place &btwo thatch blocks&r side by side, then interact with the blocks while holding the &aLarge Raw Hide.&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Loom
quests.subtitle: You'll need to work harder if you want to sleep...
desc: To make a better bed, you'll need to create some textiles. The &3Loom&r is the work-station of choice for doing this, as it allows you to create different textiles that each have different uses.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Unrefined Paper
quests.subtitle: Time to make some history.
desc: &aUnrefined Paper&r is one step away from becoming real, usable &dPaper.&r There are a lot of ways to go about crafting paper, some could be easier to do while others can be considerably more difficult depending on resource availability. Check the &bPapermaking&r entry on your &2Field Guide!&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Burlap Cloth
quests.subtitle: Made out of Jute or Flax!
desc:
You can create &dBurlap Cloth&r by soaking &aJute&r in a sealed barrel of water and weaving the resulting &aJute Fiber&r on the &3Loom&r (12 fibers per cloth).

In this pack burlap matters: Create's belts, spouts, funnels, tunnels and pulleys take burlap cloth (or leather), and the sewing table uses it too.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Wool Cloth
quests.subtitle: Baaa...
desc:
By shearing some friendly &2wool-producing&r livestock (or scraping a sheepskin hide), you can spin the resulting wool into &dWool Yarn&r with a &3Spindle&r. Working 16 yarn in a &3Loom&r gives you &dWool Cloth.&r

Besides rolling glass in &bGlassworking&r, it's used for beds and on the sewing table.

Wool is considered a &bHigh Quality Cloth.&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Silk Cloth
quests.subtitle: Very, very smooth.
desc:
&dSilk Cloth&r is woven on the &3Loom&r from 24 &aString&r, which you get from killing &bSpiders&r underground. No silkworms exist yet, sorry! Much later, GregTech's wiremill spins Polycaprolactam (nylon) into string.

Silk Cloth can stand in for wool cloth in some recipes, such as beds.

Silk Cloth is considered a &bHigh Quality Cloth.&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Beds
quests.subtitle: Rest your weary soul.
desc: Utilizing a &bHigh Quality Cloth&r, such as &aWool&r or &aSilk Cloth&r, you can create your very own &dBed.&r Unlike the &2Thatch Bed&r, a real &dBed&r is comfortable enough to sleep through the night. Sweet Dreams!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Mining Preparations
quests.subtitle: Hope you remember where you found those ore indicators!
desc:
Progressing beyond the stone age will require a lot of metal, and just picking up small ores on the surface won't be enough. You'll have to dig down and begin mining.
Assuming you &odid&r mark the place where you found your copper, find the rough middle of where the ore pieces were and start digging! It might be pretty deep, but you'll eventually strike it rich. A Prospector's Pick helps you home in on the vein. The next page has some equipment you'll want to bring along for your first mining trip!
{@pagebreak}

&lPickaxe&r: Pretty obvious what this does, you'll need a way to break the stone and harvest the ore. Cast a copper pickaxe head in a mold.

&lLadders and Torches&r: You'll need some way to climb back up out of the hole and see what you're doing!

&lSupport Beams and Planks&r: Mining here is much more dangerous - not only do monsters spawn underground, but carelessly digging around can cause a cave-in! The next quest goes over how to mitigate dangers while mining.

Now go and dig your hole, diggy diggy hole!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Mining Hazards
quests.subtitle: Thought the surface was difficult? Think again.
desc: Besides the monsters, the biggest challenge when mining is dealing with cave-ins. Mining raw rock near rock that isn't supported can start a collapse, and once one has started even supported rock can come down. Rock with a solid block beneath it is supported, and cave roofs are naturally supported. The safest thing you can do is just mine the floor, but if you want to safely mine anything else you'll have to learn how to use support beams! These are crafted from logs and a saw.
{@pagebreak}

Placing a support beam on a block raises a vertical column up to three tall, and horizontal beams connect two vertical ones up to five blocks apart. Only the horizontal beams support rock: anything within a 9 x 5 x 9 area around them. The field guide's Support Beams page has diagrams.

Ore that collapses drops a grade (rich becomes normal, normal becomes poor), so support your veins!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Panning
quests.subtitle: Re-experience the gold rush!
desc: Along riverbeds and lakebeds, you may notice gravel with specks of minerals, known as &aOre Deposits&r. Use a &bPan&r (knapped from clay and fired) on one, then stand in water and hold right-click to pan it. With luck you'll get &dsmall pieces of ore&r (native copper, native silver, native gold or cassiterite), sometimes a loose rock or even a gem. These can come in a pinch when you're missing a few millibuckets to fill a mold.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Sluices
quests.subtitle: Panning on Steroids
desc: A &3Sluice&r, made from sticks and lumber, processes those &aore deposits&r in a faster, slightly automated way: water must flow through it, and deposits dropped into the stream wash onto it and come out the bottom as ore, rocks or gems, with slightly better ore odds than panning. Check the &2Field Guide&r entry for the water setup!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: The Forge
quests.subtitle: The Fabric doesnt exist by the way.
desc:
The Forge is a crafting station used to heat materials to high temperatures. It heats things considerably faster than the Pit Kiln, and is much easier to control too.

To make the forge, surround a charcoal pile of 7 or 8 layers with 5 stone blocks (raw rock, cobblestone and the like) and light it. It needs open air above it and a view of the sky. The Forge doesn't burn logs; it burns Charcoal or Coal (bituminous coal or lignite), and a Bellows makes it hotter.

Check the field guide for walkthroughs on how to make a Charcoal Pit and a Charcoal Forge.
{@pagebreak}

In this pack a Create basin set on a charcoal forge is Create's heat source: 750 °C and up counts as heated and 2000 °C (a forge with bellows) as superheated, for heated mixing and alloying in the basin.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Raw Rock
quests.subtitle: No, it isn't just "Stone"
desc:
To create your Copper Anvil you'll need both a basic Stone Anvil and a Charcoal Forge. To make a Stone Anvil, you will need a block of Raw &6Igneous&r rock: granite, diorite, gabbro, andesite, basalt, dacite or rhyolite.

To obtain Raw Rock you can carefully break the blocks &laround&r the Raw Rock you want to mine. Once all 6 sides of the Raw Rock are exposed to air, it'll pop off into its Item form. An exposed block in the world works too: right-click its top face with a hammer to turn it into your Stone Anvil.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Rock Anvil
quests.subtitle: This won't last long
desc: Anvils are the foundation of all early game metal working. To create a proper metal anvil, you'll need to weld ingots using the previous tier of Anvil. Since Copper is the first tier, you have to use a Rock Anvil to weld them. Make one by right-clicking the top face of a block of raw igneous rock with a hammer. Welding ingots is the only thing it can do, unfortunately - you'll need the metal's proper anvil to shape them into anything else.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Fluxstones
quests.subtitle: It's basically metal glue
desc:
Flux is an item that is primarily used in metal working to weld things together, and later in the blast furnace, leather making and glass.
Some rocks - Chalk, Dolomite, Limestone and Marble - can be turned into Flux, as can shells, scutes and barnacles: craft one with any hammer (even a stone one) for 2 flux, or grind it in a Quern.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Quern and Handstone
quests.subtitle: Your first step into ore processing
desc:
The Quern and Handstone are two big rocks grinding against each other to break down materials. The bottom piece is called a Quern while the top piece is called a Handstone. The quern takes three smooth stone, which you make by chiseling raw rock, so it comes once you've cast a metal chisel.

The Quern grinds Flux, Flour, Bone Meal, Salt, dyes and mineral powders such as sulfur and redstone. Don't grind your metal ores in it: here its ore powders don't melt, and crushed ore comes from Create's millstone and GregTech's macerator instead.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Welding Copper
quests.subtitle: So close to the Copper Anvil
desc:
Light up your Forge and give it at least 2 Copper Ingots. Keep an eye on their tooltip as they heat up - once they get hot, it'll show "Can Work", but we need to wait until they get to "Can Weld", which is just before their melting point.

Once they reach it, quickly move them from the forge into the Rock Anvil's interface (the two left slots), along with at least one Flux. Then use a hammer on the anvil to weld the two ingots together while they're still hot. A barrel of water cools your new double ingot down quickly.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Fuel Temperatures
quests.subtitle: There's more than charcoal!
desc:
You may have noticed that different fuels burn at different temperatures: a fuel's tooltip tells you. Charcoal and lignite burn at 1350 °C and bituminous coal at 1415 °C, well above the melting points of bronze (950 °C) and copper (1080 °C), so keep an eye on your ingots' temperature and take them out once they can be worked or welded.

&9Note&r: putting a mold or vessel on the right side of the forge interface will catch any metals that melt.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Bellows
quests.subtitle: Higher temperatures can be reached, at a small price.
desc: The bellows forces air into the firepit or forge in front of it (or in front and one block down), raising its maximum temperature for a short time at the cost of burning fuel faster.
Charcoal burns at 1350 °C: not quite hot enough to fire pottery in a forge (1399 °C), and iron melts at 1535 °C. The bellows makes up the difference. Bituminous coal burns at 1415 °C on its own.
Made from lumber and leather. TFC's blast furnace needs one too.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Candles
quests.subtitle: Cozy...
desc: Candles are a better light source than torches: a candle burns for 240 in-game hours (ten days) before it needs relighting, a torch for 72.
Seal string in a barrel of tallow to make them (cook blubber in a pot of water for tallow), and dye them in a barrel if you like.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Bronze
quests.subtitle: Copper and tin
desc: Alloy copper (88-92%) with tin from cassiterite (8-12%) in a vessel. Bismuth bronze and black bronze work too.

quests.title: Bronze Anvil
quests.subtitle: For brass and iron
desc: A tier-2 anvil works brass and bronze; wrought iron needs it too.
Weld 14 ingots in pairs on your copper anvil (with flux) and craft the seven double ingots into the anvil. Bismuth bronze and black bronze make tier-2 anvils as well, but don't mix the three.
Bronze also opens Create (andesite alloy takes bronze nuggets) and GregTech's bronze steam machines.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Brass
quests.subtitle: Copper and zinc
desc: Alloy copper (88-92%) with zinc from sphalerite (8-12%). Brass is Create's precision metal and the airship metal.

quests.title: Glass Bottles
quests.subtitle: Not as cool as a leather flask
desc:
Glass bottles are a sturdier way to carry water: a silica glass bottle holds 500 mB, five drinks, and the other glasses a little less. However, blowing glass bottles won't be possible until you can shape Brass: a bottle is blown on a blowpipe, pinched with Jacks (two welded brass rods) and cut with a Gem Saw (a brass rod and gem powder).

Check the field guide's Glassworking pages for glass batches and the blowpipe.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Welding Bronze
quests.subtitle: I told you to get used to it
desc: Get at least 14 ingots of one kind of bronze and weld them in pairs on your copper anvil (with flux) into seven double ingots.
The tier-2 anvil can be made from bronze, bismuth bronze or black bronze, but not a mixture of the three.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Anvil Recycling?
quests.subtitle: Because 14 ingots is a lot now
desc:
Once you craft the next tier of Anvil (such as going from Copper to Bronze, or Bronze to Wrought Iron), the previous tier basically becomes useless.

However, since it's made out of metal, you &ocan and should&r melt the previous tier of Anvil back into its liquid metal form!
Grab a Vessel and place it on the right hand side of the Charcoal Forge interface, then place the Anvil and slowly heat it until it reaches the melting temperature. The molten metal will be deposited inside the Vessel, then you can cast it back into ingots or whatever you like!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Fire Clay Ingredients
quests.subtitle: The TerraFirmaCraft Rite of Passage.
desc: Fire clay is a special clay made of kaolinite, graphite and regular clay that stands up to very high temperatures. It makes the crucible, a better vessel for melting and alloying metal, and fire bricks: GregTech's steam machines are built with them, and TFC's blast furnace, the way to steel, needs them too.
You'll likely need to travel far, far away from your base for both graphite and kaolin clay, so preparation is key!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Kaolin Source: Overworld
quests.subtitle: Welcome to the Jungle
desc: Kaolin clay is found at high altitudes, in plateaus, old mountains, rolling hills and highlands, where the temperature is at least 18 °C and rainfall at least 300 mm. Blood lilies grow on it, so look out for them.

TFC: Real World's climate follows the real Earth, so think warm, wet uplands, mostly in the tropics and subtropics. From a temperate start that is a long expedition: bring plenty of food and water, a boat if there's sea in the way, and storage for bringing home as much kaolin as you can.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Kaolin Clay
quests.subtitle: Kaolin Trek: The Next Generation
desc: Once you find kaolin clay, bring back as much as you can carry! Only 20% of it turns into kaolinite powder when heated (500 °C), so it's worth firing it on the spot in pit kilns to save inventory space.

Each fire clay takes four kaolinite powder, about twenty kaolin clay, and GregTech's steam machines keep asking for fire bricks long after the crucible and blast furnace are built. Bring home more than you think you'll need, to avoid a repeat journey.
P.S.: If you've found blood lilies but no clay, try digging down a little further! Sometimes it lies a little underground.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Graphite Source: Overworld
quests.subtitle: You mean I can't just rely on surface indicators?
desc: Graphite forms in metamorphic rock: gneiss, marble, quartzite and schist, below y=60.
Its veins leave no loose pieces on the surface, so explore caves in those rocks and bring a prospector's pick. A metal shield and a spyglass can prove very useful too.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Graphite
quests.subtitle: Pencils do not exist
desc: Once you find graphite, bring back as much as you can, though you'll need far less of it than kaolin clay.
Grind it in a quern: one graphite gives four graphite powder, enough for one fire clay.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Fire Clay
quests.subtitle: At last
desc: Heat kaolin clay to get kaolinite powder. You can use a forge to heat it, but cooking big batches in pit kilns may be faster.
Grind graphite in a quern for graphite powder.
Finally, combine 4 graphite powder, 4 kaolinite powder and 1 clay ball to make fire clay.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Crucible
quests.subtitle: Melt metals like a pro
desc: The crucible sits on top of a charcoal forge (any heat source below works). It has 9 slots, holds 4000 mB of metal and shows your alloy ratios as you go. It keeps its contents when broken, and it also collects pig iron when placed below a blast furnace.
Keep in mind that the crucible WILL try to alloy everything inside it - it does not keep metals separate like a TC Smeltery - so it's a good idea to keep it clean when you aren't using it.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Fire Clay products
quests.subtitle: Extremely Heat Resistant Clay
desc: Just like regular clay, fire clay can be knapped into things that you'll then need to fire (1399 °C). Most importantly, it makes the crucible and fire bricks.
Fire ingot molds break only 1 time in 100, against 1 in 10 for a clay ingot mold.

You can also make a mold table and casting channels: connect mold tables to a crucible with channels to cast into several molds at once. Use the channel next to the crucible to start pouring, or give it a redstone pulse.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Mining in the Metallurgy Age
quests.subtitle: ROCK AND STONE!
desc: Extracting valuable resources from the ground is a major part of this modpack, and you will consume a &llot&r of metal from here on. One way to mine a lot of it at once is a GregTech mining hammer: it breaks a 3x3 area at a slower speed. Hold sneak to break single blocks.
The spade does the same for dirt, sand and gravel. The first ones you can make, in bronze, rose gold or sterling silver, come with the bronze age.
Mind TFC's cave-ins: big holes in raw rock bring the roof down unless you put up support beams.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Redstone Devices
quests.subtitle: Detect the world around you!
desc: These brass-geared devices measure the world around you, and each gives out a redstone signal directly, no comparator needed.
The Precision Clock reads the hour, or the month after you toggle it.
The Thermometer reads the air temperature, or the heat of the device it's placed on.
The Anemometer and Weather Vane read wind speed and direction respectively.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Andesite Alloy
quests.subtitle: Create starts here
desc: In this pack andesite alloy takes TFC &6andesite, basalt, dacite, rhyolite or diorite&r (raw or cobble) plus zinc or bronze nuggets.
Craft an ingot into nine nuggets.
{@pagebreak}
&lFinding the rock&r
Loose rocks on the ground are the rock right under the soil, so they show what you're standing on.

&6Volcanic regions&r (around volcanoes, volcanic islands and rifts) are mostly andesite, basalt, dacite or rhyolite. On ordinary land about one rock area in six has one of them on top; each area is about 1,000 blocks across. Mountain ranges never do, but some have diorite on top.

&6Diorite dikes&r are everywhere: upright pipes of diorite about 30 blocks across and a few hundred blocks apart, usually topping out a few blocks under the soil. Look for speckled grey-white rock in cliffs, riverbanks, ravines and cave walls, or where loose rocks don't match the rock you dig into.

quests.title: Shafts and Cogwheels
quests.subtitle: Moving parts
desc: Shafts from andesite alloy, cogwheels from shafts and planks. TFC workbenches count as crafting tables everywhere.
Large cogwheels (a shaft or cogwheel with more planks) mesh with small ones to double or halve the speed: gear your machines up or down as they need.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Power
quests.subtitle: A water wheel
desc: Put a water wheel in a river. TFC: Real World's rivers follow real rivers.
Water wheels need flowing water. If you're far from a river, a windmill is the other way to get going.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Millstone
quests.subtitle: Grinding ore
desc: Besides Create's usual milling, it grinds TFC ores into GregTech crushed ore at TFC's own yield: a rich piece gives a crushed ore 35% of the time, a normal one 25%.
It's an automatic quern: throw items in the top and take the results out with right-click (or let a funnel pull them). It's slow when turned slowly, so gear it up.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Belts
quests.subtitle: Leather or burlap
desc: TFC worlds have no vanilla kelp, so belts, the spout, funnels, tunnels and pulleys take leather, burlap cloth or dried kelp.

quests.title: Mechanical Pump
quests.subtitle: The steam age needs it
desc: Every GregTech boiler is built around a Create mechanical pump, so GregTech's steam age starts here.

It also moves fluids, from tanks and source blocks into Create's or GregTech's pipes, which work differently. Create's pipes hold no fluid themselves, need a pump to move anything and reach 16 blocks from it; a wrench turns a pipe into a straight window pipe so parallel pipes don't join. GregTech's pipes have their own buffer, keep fluid moving without a pump once it's inside, and connect only where you open them with a wrench.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Brass Casing
quests.subtitle: Precision machinery
desc: A brass sheet on a stripped log (TFC logs count). Propellers, smart machines and airships build on it.

quests.title: Mechanical Press
quests.subtitle: Heavy machines
desc: Takes a TFC wrought iron double sheet. Presses ingots into GregTech plates one for one (by hand, GregTech takes two ingots per plate).
Over a basin it compacts the basin's contents instead of pressing single items.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Encased Fan
quests.subtitle: Bulk smelting
desc: Blowing through lava or fire smelts items like a furnace: crushed copper becomes copper ingots. Crushed iron ores become cast iron; only the bloomery makes wrought iron.
Blowing through water washes items instead, but it doesn't clean GregTech crushed ore here: wash that in a cauldron or an ore washer.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Mechanical Saw
quests.subtitle: Wires
desc: Slits a GregTech plate into two single wires (copper, tin, red alloy, gold, ...), GregTech's wiremill rate without electricity.
On a moving contraption it fells trees; facing up, it cuts blocks like a stonecutter.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Crushing Wheels
quests.subtitle: Ore at GregTech's rate
desc: Crushing wheels are a 5x5 recipe, so they're built with mechanical crafters. They crush TFC ores into GregTech crushed ore at the macerator's rate, twice TFC's yield: a rich piece gives a crushed ore 70% of the time.

quests.title: Windmills
quests.subtitle: Pairs well with tulips
desc: No river nearby? A windmill turns anywhere it has room. Build at least eight sails (wool, sticks and andesite alloy) onto a windmill bearing and right-click the bearing to start it; every eight more sails add speed.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Large Water Wheels
quests.subtitle: Larger, stronger, more expensive
desc: Large water wheels give four times a small wheel's stress capacity per RPM, but still need flowing water from a river. Wrap a water wheel in eight more planks to make one.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Metal Casings
quests.subtitle: Primitive Machine Hull?
desc: Andesite casing (andesite alloy applied to a stripped log; TFC logs count) is the basis of most of Create's simple machines: gearboxes, the millstone, the press, the fan, the saw and more. Check EMI for everything you can build with it.
New to Create? There are many tutorials online about different kinds of contraptions you can build, and most of them work here too.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Tools of the Trade
quests.subtitle: These may be useful
desc: A wrench rotates Create blocks, and sneak + right-click picks them up (an axe or pickaxe still breaks them too). Create's wrench takes gold sheets and a cogwheel; any GregTech wrench completes this quest as well.
The goggles let you see much more about your machines, such as how much stress they produce or use. They're optional for now, but will prove very useful later.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Mechanical Harvester
quests.subtitle: Robotic Cherrypicking
desc: Too lazy to harvest and replant your crops? Mount harvesters on a moving contraption and they'll pick mature crops and replant them as they pass.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Early Logistics
quests.subtitle: Public infrastructure for your items
desc: You can now move your items around! Chutes drop items straight down into whatever is below them (an encased fan can push them up). Funnels pull items out of, or put them into, inventories and belts. Hoppers work too: GregTech makes them from iron plates, TFC from steel sheets.
Chutes and hoppers can also push items from containers into GregTech's item pipes.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Rotation Speed Controller
quests.subtitle: No more manual gear ratios!
desc: The &3Rotation Speed Controller&r can simplify all of your cogwheel spaghetti into a single block, letting you adjust RPM in a simple, compact way. These will be useful later when you have more machines to balance your stress units between!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Schematicannon
quests.subtitle: Automatic building
desc: The &6Schematicannon&r is an automatic building machine: it places blocks from attached containers according to a schematic, firing gunpowder as it goes. Use it to bring over buildings made in a creative world, or to copy and paste parts of your own structures.
Draw schematics with Create's schematic and quill, and write them out at a schematic table.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Copper Diving Equipment
quests.subtitle: If mining wasn't dangerous enough
desc: Struggling with aquifers in your ore veins? Create's copper diving helmet, backtank and boots let you work underwater. A full backtank holds 900 air, fifteen minutes of breathing; place it and give it rotation to fill it.
Later, red steel armour welded onto the copper pieces turns them into netherite diving gear.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Staying Organized
quests.subtitle: You're already in the first circle of microcrafting hell
desc: Struggling to keep up with all the recipes and items you need? Here's a couple of options which may help:
&3Clipboard&r: a portable to-do list, letting you check off items as you like.
&3Crafting Blueprint&r: hang it on a wall and set a recipe on it, then craft that recipe straight from your inventory without looking it up in EMI.
&3EMI favourites&r: press A while hovering over an item in EMI to add it to your favourites. It works on recipe outputs too, to keep the whole recipe.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Electron Tube
quests.subtitle: Ultra Ultra Low Voltage...?
desc: An &9Electron Tube&r is polished rose quartz on a wrought iron sheet. Rose quartz is nether quartz crafted with eight redstone; polish it with sand paper.
Quartz comes from grinding TFC rock: a millstone finds a little in raw quartzite, crushing wheels more in diorite. A quern grinds TFC cinnabar or cryolite into redstone.
Deployers and mechanical crafters are built with them.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Deployers
quests.subtitle: Primitive Assembly Line
desc: A deployer is a mechanical hand: it uses whatever it holds on the block or item in front of it. Create's sequenced assembly runs on deployers; that's how precision mechanisms and train tracks are made.
While you could get by with a single deployer, we &3really&r don't recommend it. Setting up a line of deployers along a belt will save heaps of time and sanity.
Airship envelopes also cost fewer brass nuggets when a deployer makes them.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Mechanical Crafter
quests.subtitle: For those extra large crafting recipes
desc: Mechanical crafters build Create's oversized recipes: set out enough of them in the recipe's shape, give them rotation and put one ingredient in each.
You'll want them for Create's &3Crushing Wheels&r, whose 5x5 recipe needs them. The wheels grind TFC ore at the macerator's rate.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Trains
quests.subtitle: Waypoints wishes it was as cool as these
desc: Trains are a fantastic option when it comes to any sort of long distance transportation, whether that's players, items, or fluids! They can also safely travel through unloaded chunks. On a real-scale Earth, where Rome to Naples is 9,500 blocks, a rail network pays for itself.

Tracks come out of sequenced assembly, so you'll need deployers; stations and controls start from train casing (brass casing with an obsidian plate). Steam 'n' Rails adds more tracks and locometal train parts, and its locometal boilers take GregTech coke.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Create Logistics
quests.subtitle: "We have AE2 at home"
desc: Is your chest monster starting to grow out of control? Create's logistics can help: a &3Packager&r boxes up items from an inventory, belts, chain conveyors and frogports carry the packages, and stock links let you order from your whole storage at once.
Factory Logistics does the same for fluids, in jars. Hold W over any of these items for Create's Ponder scenes.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Stock Ticker
quests.subtitle: Waiter! Waiter! More Silty Loam Rooted Dirt, please!
desc:
You now have access to &6centralized, searchable storage&r!

A basic setup is straightforward: you only need a &eStock Ticker&r, a &eStock Link&r and a &ePackager&r, as well as somewhere to put everything, such as a large &9Vault&r.

Hold &eW&r over any of them to Ponder how they work.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Factory Gauge
quests.subtitle: Automation, reinvented
desc:
&bFactory Gauges&r can do two things:

1) Monitor levels of items attached to a connected Packager
2) Automatically order crafting requests when those levels drop below a certain amount.

You heard that right, Gauges enable &6autocrafting&r! Hold &eW&r over one to Ponder a full breakdown of how to use them.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Bloomery
quests.subtitle: The only way to wrought iron
desc: Built from eight bronze double sheets, with charcoal and iron ore inside.
Wrought iron comes only from the bloomery: anything iron that is smelted or melted (GregTech's furnaces, Create's fan, TFC heat) becomes cast iron.

Set the bloomery in a chimney of stone blocks; a full chimney holds 48 items. Throw in iron ore (hematite, limonite, magnetite, or any iron item, even cast iron ingots) with charcoal: each bloom takes 100 mB of cast iron and two charcoal. Light it and wait 12 hours, then mine the bloom for raw iron blooms and work them on a bronze anvil into refined blooms and then wrought iron ingots. The field guide shows the build.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Wrought Iron
quests.subtitle: Iron means wrought iron
desc: Refine the bloom on the anvil. In this pack every iron ingot, plate and rod is TFC wrought iron.

quests.title: Wrought Iron Double Sheet
quests.subtitle: For the press
desc: Weld two wrought iron sheets. Create's mechanical press needs one.

quests.title: Blast Furnace
quests.subtitle: Pig iron
desc: TFC's blast furnace turns iron ore, charcoal and flux into pig iron. GregTech's electric blast furnace is later built from one.

Craft it from a crucible and eight wrought iron double sheets, then build its chimney on top from reinforced fire bricks (a fire bricks block and a wrought iron or steel sheet): eight per layer, up to five layers, each layer holding four more ore. Put a bellows on one side, a tuyere in its interface, and a crucible right below it to catch the molten pig iron.

Drop in equal numbers of iron ore and flux, plus charcoal: it burns only charcoal (coke is for GregTech's primitive blast furnace). Light it, keep it fuelled, and work the bellows once it's as hot as charcoal gets. The field guide has the full build.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Pig Iron
quests.subtitle: On the way to steel
desc: Cast the blast furnace's molten pig iron into ingots. Pig iron is the only way to steel, whether worked on the anvil or refined in GregTech's primitive blast furnace.

quests.title: Steel
quests.subtitle: Only from pig iron
desc: Work pig iron on the anvil into high-carbon steel and then steel, or refine pig iron with charcoal or coke in GregTech's primitive blast furnace.

quests.title: This... is a Bucket.
quests.subtitle: Dear God...
desc: Three iron plates and a hammer make a vanilla bucket. In this pack iron plates are wrought iron: hammer them by hand (two ingots per plate) or press them one for one in Create's mechanical press.

TFC's buckets can't do what this one does: the wooden bucket can't carry lava, and neither it nor the red and blue steel buckets can place source blocks. The vanilla bucket does both, which makes it the way to set up lava for Create's encased fan.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: T5 Anvil: Black Steel
quests.subtitle: Tier V
desc: With the black steel anvil you can work black steel ingots into tools, armour and parts.
GregTech doesn't wait for it in this pack: high-pressure steam and LV electrics need only steel. Dive into industry now, or finish the last tier of anvils first.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: T4 Anvil: Steel
quests.subtitle: A huge leap from wrought iron
desc:
With the Steel Anvil, you'll be able to work Steel Ingots into different forms.

Steel tools and equipment have a significant boost over their bronze and wrought iron counterparts, so they're worth making if your existing ones are about to break. You'll be needing to create a lot of alloys soon, so some new mining equipment would be a wise investment.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: T3 Anvil: Wrought Iron
quests.subtitle: Sheets for heavy machines
desc: With the wrought iron anvil (tier III) you can work wrought iron ingots into sheets, tool heads and more.

Wrought iron sheets are what this pack's heavy machines are made of: Create's mechanical press (a double sheet), saw, harvester and chute, and TFC's blast furnace with its reinforced fire bricks all need them.

Wrought iron tools and armour aren't much of an improvement over bronze, but they last far longer. The next anvil is a big step up in difficulty, so this is a good point to settle down and catch up on the rest of your base.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Fully Stacked Blast Furnace
quests.subtitle: The completed Blast Furnace
desc: A blast furnace's chimney can be five layers tall, each a ring of eight reinforced fire bricks. Every layer holds four more ore, so a full one smelts twenty at a time.
It's worth building it up: you'll need a lot of steel.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Coke Oven
quests.subtitle: Finally, No More Charcoal Piles
desc: The coke oven is your first GregTech multiblock! It needs no fuel: it bakes a log into charcoal and 250 mB of creosote, or coal (TFC bituminous coal counts) into coke and 500 mB of creosote, and holds up to 32 buckets of creosote.
Charcoal feeds the forge, the bloomery and TFC's blast furnace; coke refines pig iron into steel in GregTech's primitive blast furnace. Creosote turns planks into treated wood.
Press U (uses) on the coke oven in EMI to see how to build it.
{@pagebreak}

Coke ovens can be fully automated with a coke oven hatch on their side: the hatch works as both input and output, for items and fluids. A crate for the input, a chest for the output and a drum or tank for the creosote make a simple one-way coke oven.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Weak Steel Ingredients
quests.subtitle: Hope you like math
desc: Weak steel is one half of black steel. Alloy it in a crucible from 2 parts steel, 1 part nickel and 1 part black bronze.
The exact ranges are 50-70% steel, 15-25% nickel and 15-25% black bronze; EMI shows them on molten weak steel.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Black Steel Ingredients
quests.subtitle: Conservation of matter does not apply
desc: The final two anvils are made of complex alloys that take a lot of metal. Weld weak steel and pig iron into high carbon black steel, then work it on the anvil into black steel.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Red and Blue Steel
quests.subtitle: Some of the oldest modded Minecraft fantasy steels
desc: The final tier of anvil can be made of either red or blue steel. Both are complex alloys of black steel, steel and two more metals: brass and rose gold for red steel, bismuth bronze and sterling silver for blue.
Red steel has one more use here: welded onto Create's copper diving gear, red steel armour turns it into netherite diving gear.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Weak Red Steel Ingredients
quests.subtitle: This is getting a little ridiculous
desc: Like before, weak red steel is the first step of red steel. Alloy it from 4 parts black steel, 2 parts steel, 1 part brass and 1 part rose gold.
The exact ranges are 50-55% black steel, 20-25% steel and 10-15% each of brass and rose gold.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Weak Blue Steel Ingredients
quests.subtitle: This is getting out of hand.
desc: Like before, weak blue steel is the first step of blue steel. Alloy it from 4 parts black steel, 2 parts steel, 1 part bismuth bronze and 1 part sterling silver.
The exact ranges are 50-55% black steel, 20-25% steel and 10-15% each of bismuth bronze and sterling silver.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Red Steel Ingredients
quests.subtitle: Minecraft is not a physics simulator
desc: Red steel first starts as high carbon red steel: weld weak red steel and black steel together, then work it on the anvil into red steel.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Blue Steel Ingredients
quests.subtitle: Lavoisier is rolling in his grave
desc: Blue steel first starts as high carbon blue steel: weld weak blue steel and black steel together, then work it on the anvil into blue steel.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: T6 Anvil: Red or Blue Steel
quests.subtitle: It's over
desc: The final tier of anvil! A red or blue steel anvil (tier VI) works both red and blue steel ingots.
This is the top of TerraFirmaCraft's metalworking; from here on, GregTech carries the metal.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Steel Crate
quests.subtitle: That's a lot of space!
desc: Steel Crates are a big upgrade over wooden and bronze crates or walls of chests, boasting a whopping &672&r inventory slots.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Stonecutters
quests.subtitle: Decorate your builds!
desc: The Stonecutter turns blocks into their decorative versions in one step, without chiselling each one in the world.

It's the workshop for this pack's building mods: Create's cut and polished stones (TFC andesite, basalt, dacite and rhyolite count as andesite; TFC limestone, chalk and tuff give Create's limestone, calcite and tuff), Create Deco's bricks and catwalks, Steam 'n' Rails' locometal and Copycats+ blocks. Create's mechanical saw does the same job automatically.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Grill
quests.subtitle: Cook five at once
desc: A wrought iron grill turns a firepit into a grill: use it on a firepit. It cooks five items at once, and food cooked on it gets the Wood Grilled trait, which makes it keep a little longer.
Work a wrought iron double sheet into a grill on a wrought iron anvil.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Fire Bricks
quests.subtitle: Fireboxes
desc: Fire clay bricks, fired and set with mortar. GregTech's steam machines use them where they wanted a vanilla furnace.

Knap fire clay into unfired fire bricks and fire them at 1399 °C (a pit kiln, or a forge with bellows), then craft the bricks with mortar into fire bricks blocks. TFC's blast furnace takes them too, as reinforced fire bricks: a fire bricks block and a wrought iron sheet.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Steam Boiler
quests.subtitle: GregTech begins
desc: Bronze plates, TFC fire bricks and a Create mechanical pump. It burns logs or charcoal. Every steam machine runs on boiler steam, and later the steam turbine turns it into electricity.

There are three kinds, all built around a mechanical pump: the &3Solid&r boiler burns solid fuels like coal and charcoal, the &3Liquid&r boiler burns lava or creosote, and the &3Solar&r boiler needs no fuel but only works during the day. If you're unsure, start with the solid one.
Steam machines all have a vent which needs to stay unblocked in order for them to work properly.
{@pagebreak}

&aWarning:&r Boilers will &bexplode&r if you put water into them while they are dry and hot. It's best to always have water being piped into them, but you can always break and place the block to reset its temperature.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Steam Macerator
quests.subtitle: Twice the ore
desc: Crushes TFC ore pieces into GregTech crushed ore at twice TFC's yield: 5 small, 10 poor, 2 normal or 10 rich pieces give 1, 3, 1 or 7 crushed ores. Mineral and gem ores give 2 each.
That's twice what the millstone gives, so it's worth building even next to one. It also grinds crushed ore into impure dust and logs into wood pulp.
EMI shows more output slots than you'll get: the steam macerator has one, and byproducts from macerating wait for an &6HV&r macerator.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Ore Processing
quests.subtitle: Crushed ore
desc: Proper ore processing is a large, complex beast that you'll learn more about as you progress; it gets much more metal and other byproducts out of every ore you mine.

Crushed ore comes from Create's millstone and crushing wheels or GregTech's macerator. Wash it in a cauldron or ore washer, smelt it in a steam furnace or with Create's fan, or keep processing it for byproducts. Crushed hematite, magnetite, limonite and pyrite smelt into cast iron.
TFC's quern doesn't make crushed ore in this pack: it grinds ores into powders that don't melt, so keep your metal ores out of it.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Steam Alloy Smelter
quests.subtitle: Red alloy and rubber
desc: Runs GregTech's alloy recipes on steam: red alloy from one copper and four redstone (grind cinnabar or cryolite in a TFC quern), rubber from raw rubber and sulfur.
It also makes &6Bronze&r and &6Brass&r the effortless way: three copper and one tin or zinc, as ingots or dusts, give four ingots. No vessel, no watching temperatures.
It's a steam-hungry machine. If you find yourself running out of steam, give a machine a &alove-tap&r with a &dSoft Mallet&r to pause it.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Rubber
quests.subtitle: For cables
desc: Sticky resin from GregTech's rubber trees goes into a steam extractor for raw rubber; alloy-smelt three raw rubber with one sulfur dust (crush TFC sulfur or pyrite). Create's press turns rubber into plates.
Rubber insulates every cable from here on, so it's well worth automating.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Primitive Blast Furnace
quests.subtitle: Faster steel
desc: Refines TFC pig iron with charcoal, coal or coke into steel, faster than working it on the anvil. It takes pig iron only.

quests.title: High-Pressure Steam
quests.subtitle: Steel boilers
desc: Steel boilers make steam faster; high-pressure steam machines run at full speed.

quests.title: Item Pipes
quests.subtitle: Not as cool as Item Conduits
desc: &3Item Pipes&r are a simple yet effective way to move items around &dinstantly&r, but with throughput limits. Higher tier pipes provide ridiculously large throughput - a rare sight in modded Minecraft!
Item Pipes &9do not pull&r: they push any item inserted into them to connected inventories, prioritizing &9the closest inventory&r. Restrictive pipes are the last choice.
{@pagebreak}
For now, feed them with Create funnels, &6Chutes&r and &6Hoppers&r; in LV, Conveyor Modules, Output Buses and machine Auto-Outputs join in.
&9Note:&r pipes connect only to the block they were placed against. To open more connections, use your &5Wrench&r.
Get &eany&r of the suggested Item Pipes to complete this quest.
{@pagebreak}

&l&3Lore:&r&o Oooooh, YEAH! Item Pipes were in GregTech 5, and for whatever reason they weren't kept for GTCE, so you had to use other mods to transport items. Who does that!? We hope you enjoy Item Pipes being back in GregTech!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Fluid Pipes
quests.subtitle: Liquids, gases... we don't discriminate
desc: &bFluid Pipes&r will transport &7Steam&r and other fluids between machines for you.

Each pipe has a throughput in mB/t and a &6Temperature Limit&r. This is relevant right now, as steam will burn wooden pipes. The bigger the pipe, the &ahigher&r the throughput, but the more &dexpensive&r the craft; hover over one for its numbers.
To start off, use wooden pipes for room-temperature fluids and bronze ones for steam and anything hot.
{@pagebreak}
&aReminder:&r 1 second = 20 ticks... assuming the server isn't lagging.

&dNote:&r pipes connect only to the block they were placed against. To open more connections, use your wrench on the pipe. You can also sneak-right-click with your wrench to disable input from a side, which helps against sloshing.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Efficient Fluid Storage
quests.subtitle: I don't think a wooden barrel can hold molten steel
desc: This pack has a plethora of fluids, so you may be looking for a way to store them.

Introducing... &aDrums&r! They have large internal buffers, and any &aDrum&r can be broken and picked up and will &dkeep the fluid&r inside. A right-click with a Soft Mallet or Screwdriver lets a Drum drain its contents into a tank placed below it.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o These drums are actually ported from GregTech 6.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Multiblock Tanks
quests.subtitle: Huge amounts of fluid storage
desc: Do you have a huge pile of barrels as you try to store all that creosote?

Look no further than multiblock tanks: even the cheapest, wooden one holds far more than barrels, and there are bronze and steel versions for even more storage. Fill and drain them through the controller or a tank valve.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter metal_age

quests.title: Sticky Resin
quests.subtitle: No, it's not Rosin
desc: &dSticky Resin&r stands in for slime balls in some recipes, and goes into &aResistors&r and &aCircuit Boards&r, which you'll need a fair bit of to advance into the &7Low Voltage&r age.
GregTech's rubber trees grow in this world: chop their natural logs and they usually drop sticky resin. A steam extractor turns it into raw rubber.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Automatic Mining
quests.subtitle: Let the machines swing the pickaxe
desc: You now have two ways to mine automatically! Both of them are very slow, so it's a good idea to set them up, keep their chunks loaded (Create: Power Loader's chunk loaders) and go do something else instead of sitting and waiting.
The &3Mechanical Drill&r needs a contraption to move it, breaking all stone along the way. You can also attach it to the front of a train or minecart to dig tunnels.
{@pagebreak}

The &3Steam Miner&r, on the other hand, only breaks ore blocks (TFC's ores count) and replaces them with cobblestone, leaving the rest of the ground intact. It mines ores in a small radius, so it has to be moved less often than a drill, but it's also a lot slower.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Molding
quests.subtitle: Reduce the amount of malding by molding
desc: In addition to alloying metals together, the Alloy Smelter can also use &3Casting Molds&r to shape materials.

Molds start as an &aEmpty Mold&r: four steel plates with a hammer and a file. A hammer then shapes it into the mold you want. You'll need the &aBall&r mold for glass tubes; the &aPlate&r mold makes glass plates.
Be sure to make &aCasting Molds&r - don't make &cExtruder Molds&r, as they're used in a different machine.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Glass Tubes
quests.subtitle: You'll want a lot of these
desc: Glass tubes come out of the Alloy Smelter: one glass dust with a &aBall Casting Mold&r. Grind glass (made with TFC's glassworking) in the steam macerator for the dust.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Electronics #3: Vacuum Tubes
quests.subtitle: The harder component for circuits
desc: Crafting Vacuum Tubes might make you question your existence: a glass tube, two steel bolts and three copper wires each. They're very expensive right now, but they'll get cheaper in a moment - that's the general GregTech philosophy! The assembler makes two to four at a time.
Vacuum Tubes are also technically your first Ultra Low Voltage (&8ULV&r) Circuit! Congratulations! From here you can jump right into crafting LV Circuits.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Steam Compressor
quests.subtitle: The Steam Compressor compresses...
desc: The &3Steam Compressor&r can turn ingots and gems into blocks, nuggets into ingots, and most importantly, wood pulp into single Planks. You'll see why those are important soon!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Wood Planks
quests.subtitle: Untreated Plywood...?
desc: GregTech's &aWood Plank&r is a thin wooden plate, the base of your first circuit boards. Grind logs (TFC logs work) into wood pulp in a macerator, then press the pulp into planks in the Steam Compressor, one each.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Resin-Coated Boards
quests.subtitle: I guess you could say we're... bored of LaTeX?
desc: Coat a wood plank in sticky resin: one plank and two resin make a &aResin Circuit Board&r (three planks and six resin make three).
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Electronics #2: Circuit Boards
quests.subtitle: The easier component for circuits
desc: Surround a Resin Circuit Board with eight copper single wires to make your first &aResin Printed Circuit Board&r!
Create's mechanical saw slits a copper plate into two wires. Later the assembler makes boards from glue and copper foil instead.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Electronics #1: Resistors
quests.subtitle: The more... resistant... component for circuits
desc: Resistors are components that will be used to make your first Circuit: sticky resin, paper, copper wire and a pinch of coal or charcoal dust.
Wires may be expensive right now: Create's mechanical saw slits a copper plate into two. Once you have an LV &3Wiremill&r, switch to the recipes with &aFine Wires&r; one copper ingot makes eight.
