quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Paper
quests.subtitle: Not from sugarcane
desc: If you haven't made any yet, there are two ways to get paper without electricity.
1) Papyrus: cut it into strips with a knife, soak the strips in a barrel of water, weave four soaked strips on a loom and scrape the unrefined paper with a knife.
2) Craft it from treated hide, an egg, flour and lime.
Later, a chemical bath turns wood pulp straight into paper.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Red Alloy
quests.subtitle: A completely fictional alloy
desc: &4Red Alloy&r is an alloy of Copper and Redstone, prized in the GregTech universe for its conductivity. Make it in the Alloy Smelter: one copper and four redstone. A TFC quern grinds cinnabar or cryolite into redstone.
Press it into a plate and slit the plate into wires with Create's saw. Your first circuits need red alloy cable.
&l&3Lore:&r&o This material originally comes from RedPower - what a throwback!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Steam Forge Hammer
quests.subtitle: The Forge Hammer hammers...
desc: With the creation of this machine, many recipes that once required you to use a hammer can instead be made here, and quickly: crushed ore into impure dust, purified ore into purified dust, and gem blocks back into gems.
It also makes &aPlates&r at a better ratio than by hand: &6three Ingots for two Plates&r. (Create's press still beats it at one for one.)
It crushes vanilla cobblestone into gravel and gravel into sand, but not TFC rock. Its recipe takes a vanilla anvil, so start saving wrought iron.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Steam Furnace
quests.subtitle: The Steam Furnace furnaces...
desc: Want to quickly smelt something into an ingot? The &3Steam Furnace&r does just that! It can turn crushed ores and dusts quickly into their ingot form, at the expense of not getting any byproducts.
Iron ores (hematite, magnetite, limonite, pyrite) and iron dusts come out as TFC cast iron, as if you'd melted them; wrought iron still comes only from the bloomery.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Steam Oven
quests.subtitle: The Steam Furnace's big brother
desc: &o...or little brother. Don't let him know!&r
The &3Steam Oven&r is a great multiblock option if you need to &6effortlessly smelt large quantities of items.&r No more lines of furnaces that you have to manually empty and refuel!

It effectively behaves as a parallel furnace, smelting up to 8 items at a time for a low cost of Steam. Like every steam multiblock, its recipes take half again as long as EMI shows. Press the EMI 'Uses' key (U) on the controller to see the structure; click a block to see what fits there.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Steam Rock Crusher
quests.subtitle: The Rock Crusher duplicates blocks... wait what?
desc: The Rock Crusher is basically a cobblestone generator in a box. With lava and water next to it, it makes more of the vanilla cobblestone or stone in its slot (which isn't used up), at the low cost of just a little steam.
It only makes vanilla stone, not TFC rock, so this doesn't help at all for progression; its cobblestone can feed the forge hammer if you need vanilla gravel or sand.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Soft Mallet
quests.subtitle: Time for a break
desc: The &6Soft Mallet&r is a particularly useful tool during the steam age. Hit a GregTech machine with it to pause it, and again to start it back up.
When your boilers can't keep up, pause the machines you don't need right now so the rest get the steam.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Large Bronze Boiler
quests.subtitle: Mass producing Steam
desc: The &eLarge Bronze Boiler&r is a multiblock that makes far more &bSteam&r than the small boilers. It burns solid fuels or liquid ones such as creosote, and takes a while to heat up.
Its controller takes LV circuits. Press the EMI 'Uses' key (U) on the controller to see the structure.
Like every boiler, keep water flowing in before it gets hot, or it will &cEXPLODE&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Early Ore Processing - Part 2
quests.subtitle: Smash it with a hammer
desc:
Combine Crushed Ore with a GregTech hammer in a crafting grid to turn it into Impure Dust (TFC's hammers don't work for this). The macerator does the same, with a chance at a byproduct dust on top.

Impure dust smelts into the same ingot as the crushed ore, but it can also be washed into clean dust (next quest). This may all be slow and tedious for now, but you'll soon unlock ways to do this faster and automatically!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Early Ore Processing - Part 3
quests.subtitle: Wash that dirty dust
desc:
Finally, right-click a Cauldron of water with Impure or Purified Dust to wash it into clean Dust, your ore's final form. A cauldron takes seven wrought iron plates; later the ore washer and the centrifuge do this in bulk, with byproducts.

Clean dust smelts into an ingot, and many GregTech recipes take it directly.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Medical Conditions
quests.subtitle: Don't eat the Asbestos
desc:
Be careful what you carry! GregTech marks some materials &cHazardous&r on their tooltip (hold Shift for the details), and carrying them builds up a &6Medical Condition&r with nasty effects, up to and including &cdeath&r.

If a debuff suddenly appears, get that item out of your inventory and into a chest!
{@pagebreak}

You will eventually need to work with some of these materials, so you have ways to deal with them.

The best way is to avoid getting any conditions in the first place: GregTech's Face Mask and Rubber Gloves protect against some hazards (their tooltips list which). Many conditions fade on their own, but some are &epermanent&r; GregTech's Paracetamol and RadAway pills, made much later, are its medicine.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter stone_age

quests.title: Welcome to Ore Processing
quests.subtitle: To Process, Ore Not To Process
desc: An important part of &6GregTech&r is its &dOre Processing Mechanics&r, but it can get pretty complicated, so this chapter is here to help!

In this pack GregTech's own ore veins are off: every ore is a TFC ore. Create's millstone and crushing wheels and GregTech's macerator turn TFC ore pieces into GregTech &aCrushed Ore&r, and from there GregTech's usual chain applies. GregTech-only minerals (bauxite, galena, platinum, ...) have no veins here, so their lines don't apply.
{@pagebreak}

EMI has an &6Ore Processing Diagram&r tab: press the Show Uses key (default &bU&r) on a crushed ore and look for it. It starts from GregTech's ore blocks, which don't generate here, so start reading at crushed ore.

A major part of GregTech philosophy is that there's not just one way to solve a problem. The columns of this chapter follow an ore from raw ore to dust; the rows are the tiers that bring new machines.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Raw Ore
desc: This column shows ways to process raw ore, the first step of ore processing! Here that's TFC's ore pieces (small, poor, normal and rich, plus the mineral and gem ores); GregTech's own ore blocks and raw ores don't generate in this pack.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Crushed Ore
desc: This column shows how to process crushed ore, which is almost always the second step.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Purified Ore
desc: This column shows what to do with your purified ore.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Refined Ore
desc: The only things you can really do with refined ore are crush it into dust or smelt it.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Impure Dust
desc: Wash that dirty dust!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Purified Dust
desc: This column shows what you can do with your purified dust.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Your final dust
quests.subtitle: Or is it?
desc: &6Dusts&r are the final form of almost every ore.

From here, you can smelt it in a steam furnace or with Create's fan, send it to &estorage&r, or even start using it right away! Iron dusts smelt into TFC cast iron. Some dusts will require one last step before they become truly useful.
Remember to keep your &6ore processing line&r in top shape! You'll want to keep expanding and upgrading it as you progress, so you can spend less time mining and more time gregging.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Early Ore Processing
quests.subtitle: Before electricity
desc: This row is for the very basics of ore processing: Create's millstone and crushing wheels, a hammer in the crafting grid and a cauldron of water. There are no byproducts yet, though Create can already automate the crushing.
The millstone gives TFC's own yield; crushing wheels and the macerator give twice that.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Steam Age Ore Processing
quests.subtitle: Steam does the hammering
desc: Steam machines take over the hand work: the &3Steam Macerator&r crushes TFC ore at twice TFC's yield and crushed ore into impure dust, the &3Steam Forge Hammer&r does the hammer's crafting-grid steps, and the &3Steam Furnace&r smelts crushed ore and dusts.
Washing still means a cauldron, and byproducts wait for LV.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: &7LV&r Ore Processing
desc: LV comes with a ton of machines that can process your ores in many different ways. The most important is probably the Thermal Centrifuge.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: &bMV&r Ore Processing
desc: Not much happens at MV except that the electrolyzer becomes much more powerful.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: &6HV&r Ore Processing
desc: HV Macerators now output byproducts! If you don't have a dedicated ore processing setup yet, now is definitely the time to build one.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: &5EV&r Ore Processing
desc: EV is the first tier where you'll need to start splitting up your ore processing into different "lines".
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: &9IV&r Ore Processing
desc: With IV comes the big huge multiblocks to really ramp up your ore processing speeds.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Ore processing with GregTech's own tools
quests.subtitle: Providing answers to its own problems
desc: GregTech comes with its own tools to help solve ore processing logistics.
The &6Robot Arm&r can move precise numbers of items into a machine. The &6Tag Filter&r can filter items by tag, such as '&5*purified_ores*&r' to match all Purified Ores.

The &4Smart Filter&r can filter items depending on their &6recipe&r. For example, if you use it with a robot arm on an electrolyzer, and set the robot arm to supply exact, it will only move your dusts into the electrolyzer once it has as many inputs as the recipe requires!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Bathe them in Water
quests.subtitle: The standard option for most ores
desc: Most ores don't need any fancy bathing setups, and running them through an &dOre Washer&r will suffice: about a third of a byproduct per ore.
If you use the &bOre Washer&r, make sure to use &9Distilled Water&r to double the speed of the recipe.
Don't have one yet? You can right-click a cauldron of water with crushed ore to purify it, though this won't get you any byproducts.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Bathe them in Sodium Persulfate
quests.subtitle: Not just for circuit board etching
desc: Once you get to LV, you may be interested in using a &bChemical Bath&r with &dSodium Persulfate&r to get some extra byproducts. Not all ores can be processed this way, but the ones that can will get a &670 percent&r chance of a byproduct, compared to the &633 percent&r of the &bOre Washer&r.
Sodium persulfate comes from electrolyzing sodium bisulfate, and it can be a little annoying to mass produce.
The quest below gives the crushed ores worth the investment.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Bathe them in Mercury
quests.subtitle: Don't stick your finger in it
desc: Bathing certain ores in &dMercury&r can give some other useful byproducts. Not all ores can be processed this way, but the ones that can will get a &670 percent&r chance of a byproduct, compared to the &633 percent&r of the &bOre Washer&r.
&dMercury&r can be easily obtained by centrifuging TFC &cCinnabar&r dust (or &cRedstone&r).
The quest below gives the crushed ores worth bathing in Mercury.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Mercury bathing examples
quests.subtitle: Liquid metal bath time
desc: Here's what TFC's ores give in a Mercury bath:
- &6Crushed Gold&r: &dSilver&r
- &6Crushed Copper&r: &dGold&r
- &6Crushed Silver&r: &dGold&r
- &6Crushed Magnetite&r: &dGold&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Sodium Persulfate bathing examples
quests.subtitle: A useful time saver
desc: Here's what TFC's ores give in a Sodium Persulfate bath:
- &6Crushed Sphalerite&r: &dZinc&r
- &6Crushed Tetrahedrite&r: &dCadmium&r
- &6Crushed Limonite&r: &dCobalt Oxide&r
- &6Crushed Malachite&r: &dZincite&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: The Thermal Centrifuge
quests.subtitle: The go-to for most purified ores
desc: For all your other Purified Ores that don't need special treatment, it's best to run them through the &dThermal Centrifuge&r. This machine can produce byproducts at a reliable rate, without needing any other ingredients. It's quite slow, however, so we suggest making several.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: The Sifter
quests.subtitle: The Skyblock Simulator
desc: The &6Sifter&r should be used for all your &aGems&r: TFC's ruby, sapphire, emerald, topaz, opal, amethyst and diamond. Sifting a purified gem ore gives more gems than any other method, and it's the easiest way to get Exquisite and Flawless gems.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: The Macerator
quests.subtitle: (again)
desc: The macerator can sometimes yield different byproducts from your Purified ores than other routes, but these are still locked to &6HV&r like every other macerator byproduct.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Centrifuging the dust
quests.subtitle: Byproducts of byproducts
desc: The &6Sifter&r can output &6Purified Dust&r, which you can toss into a centrifuge for a few extra byproducts.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Electromagnetic Separator
quests.subtitle: Probably the least useful GregTech machine
desc: The &6Electromagnetic Separator&r pulls magnetic metals out of &dPurified Dusts&r, which you get by crushing purified ores. From TFC's ores: purified &6Magnetite&r dust gives some &eGold&r, and purified hematite, limonite and pyrite dust give a little &7Iron&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Further refinement
quests.subtitle: An encore for ore!
desc: Certain &6Dusts&r have no direct use and need splitting into their elements. &cRuby&r dust, for example, electrolyzes into &dChromium&r and &dAluminium&r, and clay dust gives aluminium too.
Most of these recipes will only be available with an &bMV Electrolyzer&r, so come back to this later!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: The Packer
quests.subtitle: It's real fast
desc:
Back in the old days of GregTech, this little bad boy saw a lot of use—you used to get a ton of &6Small&r and &6Tiny Dusts&r from ore processing.

Nowadays, it's only really useful for automatic packing, such as &dRare Earth&r in a &6Centrifuge&r returning many &6Small Piles of Dust&r.

Don't forget: a &eRobot Arm&r set to Supply Exact mode can be useful to avoid clogging the input slots.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Chromium
quests.subtitle: Chrome me up, choom!
desc: Getting &bChromium&r will be one of the first ore processing challenges you encounter. In this pack it comes from TFC's &cRuby&r:
- Washing crushed ruby in the &dOre Washer&r gives chromium dust a third of the time.
- Centrifuging impure ruby dust gives a little more.
- An &bMV Electrolyzer&r splits ruby dust into chromium and aluminium.
{@pagebreak}
Later, &6Ruby Slurry&r (crushed or purified ruby mixed with aqua regia) gets more chromium out of each ruby, along with aluminium.
GregTech's other chromium sources, chromite and garnet sand, have no veins here.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Molybdenum Line
quests.subtitle: Moly-b-done yet?
desc:
&bMolybdenum&r goes into the Large Centrifugal Unit's coils, RTM alloy and several &6EV&r alloys.

TFC &aMalachite&r caps copper deposits that also hold &aMolybdenite&r. Run crushed malachite through a &3Thermal Centrifuge&r, or centrifuge pure malachite dust, and molybdenite comes out as the &6Byproduct&r.

An &3Electrolyzer&r splits molybdenite dust into &bMolybdenum&r and sulfur.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Crushing with byproducts
quests.subtitle: I can get even more from my ores!
desc: While looking at &bEMI&r, you've probably noticed that your &dMacerator&r lists more &boutputs&r than what you're actually getting.

GregTech doesn't communicate this very well, but these extra slots are only available in &6HV&r. Once you make it to that tier, the &6HV&r macerator becomes incredibly powerful, giving a huge amount of bonus byproducts when it grinds crushed and purified ores.
TFC ore pieces have no byproducts at the first crush, in any machine.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: The Infamous Platline
quests.subtitle: GregTech players vs Mekanism players when they need Osmium:
desc: The &6Platinum Line&r will be your first real challenge to process, providing you with essential platinum-group metals: &bPlatinum&r, &bPalladium&r, &bRuthenium&r, &bRhodium&r, &bIridium&r, and &bOsmium&r.

GregTech's platinum-bearing ores don't generate here, so this line is the main way to get any of them. &aPlatinum Group Sludge&r comes from purified &6Tetrahedrite&r, a TFC copper ore, in a Chemical Reactor with nitric acid.
The Platline can be started at &6HV&r, but you won't be able to complete it fully until later in &5EV&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: Ore processing but bigger
quests.subtitle: When size does matter
desc: Once you get to IV, you'll gain access to multiblock versions of GregTech's single block machines. They do the exact same recipes as their single block cousins, but are more flexible - you can put lots of huge Input Buses on them, you can overclock them with higher tier &6Energy Hatches&r instead of making new ones every tier, and they even support &6Parallel Hatches&r to do multiple recipes simultaneously!
Their recipes and casings take advanced alloys, so check EMI before you commit.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter ore_proc

quests.title: LV Machine Hull
quests.subtitle: Steel and cable
desc: Steel plates and tin cable (tin wire covered in rubber). Every LV machine starts as a hull.
The LV Machine Casing is eight steel plates and a wrench; the hull adds two wrought iron plates, a steel plate and two tin cables. Try to make at least three or four to begin.
These quests mark each new tier by its machine hull. As a quick reminder, &cmachines explode when exposed to rain or water&r, so keep them under a roof.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: LV Motor
quests.subtitle: Around a Create shaft
desc: GregTech's LV motors are built around two Create shafts, with copper wire and a magnetic iron rod.

The full recipe: two Create shafts, four copper wires, two tin cables and a magnetic iron (or steel) rod. Magnetize the rod with redstone by hand, or for free in a Polarizer. Make plenty: the first LV machines take up to four motors each, and every pump and piston hides one (conveyors two).
&2EMI is your friend&r: the recipe tree button at the bottom right of a recipe breaks it down into everything it needs, and can add a shopping list to your favourites.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Steam Turbine
quests.subtitle: Electricity
desc: Electricity comes from boiler steam: feed an LV steam turbine from your boilers and cable it to your machines.
The turbine turns &d2 mB of steam into 1 EU&r: 64 mB a tick for 32 EU/t. Steam isn't energy-dense, so plan on plenty of boilers and wide pipes.
When single boilers can't keep up, a &6Large Bronze Boiler&r (LV circuits, tin cables and a bronze firebox casing) burns solid fuels, lava or creosote.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Pumps and Pistons
quests.subtitle: Create inside
desc: LV pumps contain a Create mechanical pump, LV pistons a Create cogwheel.
Pump: an LV motor, a Create mechanical pump, a tin rotor, a tin screw, two rubber rings and a tin cable. Piston: an LV motor, a Create cogwheel, three steel plates, two steel rods and two tin cables.
Both are crafting components first, but the pump is also a &9cover&r: placed on a machine it moves fluids in or out, and it takes a Fluid Filter.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Circuits
quests.subtitle: Electronic circuit
desc: Vacuum tubes, resistors and red alloy cable on a circuit board, with a steel plate. Circuits gate every LV machine.

The recipe may look intimidating, but if you've spent some time in the steam age, every part should be easy to make in bulk. You'll be making a lot of these: the assembler makes their parts cheaper, and the circuit assembler makes two circuits at a time.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Assembler
quests.subtitle: GregTech's workhorse
desc: Most of GregTech's LV recipes go through the assembler.
It's &cexpensive&r (two robot arms and two conveyor modules), but it pays back fast with better recipes:
&9-&r &6Vacuum Tubes&r: two per craft, three with molten red alloy and four with annealed copper wire too, instead of one by hand
&9-&r &6Resistors&r: two per craft with glue, four with annealed copper fine wire
&9-&r &6Circuit Boards&r: four copper foils and glue instead of eight copper wires
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Electric Blast Furnace
quests.subtitle: The next tier
desc: Built from TFC's blast furnace, heat-proof invar casings and LV circuits. It needs cupronickel coils and electricity to run.

Your &efirst electric multiblock&r: three TFC blast furnaces, three LV circuits, a heat-proof casing and two tin cables make the controller. It processes materials at high temperatures; its main job now is &aAluminium&r (1700K), on the way to &bMV&r.

It's a beefy boy: every recipe needs at least &9120 EU/t&r, almost four &7LV&r generators. Two LV energy hatches let it draw up to 128 EU/t. Keep the generators close and use thick cable (2x tin cable or better), or cable loss will make it flicker.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849

quests.title: Potin Seller...
quests.subtitle: ...I'm going into battle, and I need only your finest Potin.
desc: &dPotin Fluid Pipes&r carry plenty of fluid for an early pipe (check the tooltip for the numbers). You may want to look into making some of these to aid with fluid logistics.

Potin is six copper, two tin and one lead: craft its &eDust&r form by hand, then smelt it. TFC has no lead ore; lead is a byproduct of silver, from washing crushed silver in the &3Ore Washer&r or centrifuging impure silver dust.
This quest calls for any size of potin pipe.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o &dPotin Fluid Pipes&r were originally created in &9GT++&r, and were a huge power spike for players in a little pack called &4GT:NH&r.
In the real world, &dPotin&r is an alloy used in coins, not pipes. GTCEu just gets more unrealistic by the day...
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Steam Grinder
quests.subtitle: The Steam Macerator's little sister
desc: Like the Steam Oven, the &3Steam Grinder&r is a multiblock version of a single machine, the macerator, that can do up to 8 items at the same time. Its recipe takes two potin gears. Is it worth it? That's totally up to you.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: Super Chests and Super Tanks
quests.subtitle: Super Storage Drawers
desc: This is the &cu&6l&et&ai&bm&9a&5t&4e&r portable item and storage solution if you have a lot of single items or fluids. While the first (&7LV&r) Super Chests and Tanks start out relatively small, higher tiers, and the Quantum Chests and Tanks after them, can hold an insane amount of stuff - all in one single block without any regard to temperature or acidity!

Like Drums, Super Tanks and Chests &6keep their contents when broken&r, can be cleared in the crafting grid, and can automatically void any overflow. Unlike drums, however, Super Tanks also &asafely contain&r their contents, preventing you from getting burnt, frozen, or floating.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter steam_age

quests.title: LV Fluid Regulator
quests.subtitle: A cover that you may not use much
desc:
The &aFluid Regulator&r is sort of the equivalent to a &9Robot Arm&r for Fluids.

It can transfer fluids, but has two useful modes:

&9-&r &dSupply Exact&r will transfer the amount of specified Fluid per tick if available. No more, no less.
&9-&r &dKeep Exact&r will make sure the exact amount of Fluid in the attached machine is being kept.

You won't need it much, because natively GT machines will fill only one slot with the &6Pump Cover&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: LV Robot Arm
quests.subtitle: You're going to hate making these
desc:
When placed on a machine, Robot Arms are a more configurable version of a Conveyor Module. They allow you to transfer items in specific batches, at specific rates, or keep a certain amount of items stocked.

&9Note:&r The functionalities provided by the Robot Arm work &lonly&r if it is &lrequired&r to perform the operation.
{@pagebreak}

&l&3Lore:&r&o GregTech 5 had blocks such as the Buffer, Filter and Type Filter to allow fine control over items. In GTCE it's all been replaced by the almighty Robot Arm and various Filter Covers. Much more compact!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: LV Conveyor Module
quests.subtitle: A crafting component, but also a cover!
desc:
Less common as a component, but used in a number of critical machines.

When placed on a machine, conveyor modules will transfer items. You can configure them to import or export.

They can also accept various &9Item Filters&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: But what are Amps?
quests.subtitle: Amps and You: a how-to
desc:
This questline serves as a quick guide to &9GregTech Amperage&r.

&6&lTL;DR:&r For safety, match the Amperage limit of your Cables with the max amount of Amps provided by your Energy Producers.

Still confused? Check the &cGregTech Power&r chapter for a full rundown on GregTech's electricity system, voltage tiers included!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Your first Aluminium Ingot
quests.subtitle: We're basically in MV now, right?
desc:
Well... can you show us an &bMV&r Circuit as well?

&aAluminium&r is the main ingredient for &bMV&r machinery. Get ready to need a lot of it. The EBF smelts aluminium dust at &c1700K&r, so Cupronickel Coils (1800K) are just hot enough.

Smelting takes about a third less time with &9Nitrogen&r, which you get by centrifuging &9Air&r from a &3Gas Collector&r.

&6You will still need MV Circuits in order to make MV machines!&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Battery Preparations!
quests.subtitle: Batteries are great!
desc:
Make some &aBattery Alloy&r, used for Battery Hulls: mix 4 lead dust with 1 antimony dust in a Mixer.

Neither has its own ore here. &aLead&r is a byproduct of TFC native silver (macerate its crushed ore), and &aAntimony&r one of tetrahedrite.

A Battery Hull is two battery alloy plates and a tin cable.

&9Note:&r This quest does &lnot&r contain functional Batteries - head on for that.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Cover Behaviour
quests.subtitle: Extra utility without taking up blockspace!
desc:
Covers are placed by right-clicking with Cover in hand on a face of a machine, and removed with a &5Crowbar&r (or by mining the machine, but that's way slower).

Pretty much any GregTech Tile-Entity will accept Covers, even if they wouldn't provide any functionality.

Opening a Cover is done by sneak-right-clicking it with an &5empty hand&r. You can also right-click with a &5Screwdriver&r, or sneak-right-click on another face using the grid.
{@pagebreak}

For Covers that transfer Items/Fluids, you will have a button to enable/disable other forms of transfer through the cover:

&9- &rDisabled: only the cover will be allowed to transfer on this machine side.

&9-&r Allow Filtered (only relevant with a filter!): other transfer will be enabled only if it matches the filter

&9-&r Allow Unfiltered: any other transfer is allowed on this machine side.

Placing a cover of a lower voltage tier on a machine is &9safe&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Machine Auto-Output Behaviour
quests.subtitle: Let's learn.
desc:
All machines typically have one &7Front Face&r, and one &9Output Face&r.

The &7Front Face&r should be obvious.
The &9Output Face&r is the face with a dot or hole on it. By default, this is at the back of the machine as you place it.

Machines can &aauto-output&r through their output face. To enable auto-output, click the appropriate button in the GUI. Fluid and item auto-outputs are toggled separately. Further control over auto-outputs can be achieved with &dFilters&r and &dCovers&r, which are explained in the &dCover Behavior&r quest found in this chapter.
{@pagebreak}

Right-clicking a machine with a &5Wrench&r changes the output side, and shift-right-clicking changes the front side. Keep in mind that the front side &ccannot&r also be the output side! 

By default, items and fluids cannot be inserted through the output side, but this can be toggled with a &5Screwdriver&r. Either right-click the output face directly, or shift-right-click on the grid corresponding to the side of the output.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Wiremill
quests.subtitle: No more painful wires!
desc: The Wiremill is a good first machine. It draws &6two Wires from one Ingot&r, the same as Create's press and saw, but in one step and on electricity. It also makes &6fine wire&r, four from a single wire, which resistors and diodes eat by the stack.
{@pagebreak}

&9Note:&r Recipes inside &3LV Machines&r go up to a maximum usage of &a32 EU/t (LV)&r. Anything higher than that and you will need a &bMV&r (or better) Machine. Needless to say, we aren't quite there yet.

You will need a &dProgrammed Circuit&r for certain recipes. We're sure you don't want to spend a precious Circuit to craft one, so &6read the dedicated quest for important details&r.

With this machine safely crafted - welcome to the age of all things electric!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Bender
quests.subtitle: The Bender bends!
desc:
Create's press already turns one ingot into one plate, but the Bender does more. It rolls a plate into &6four Foils&r (a hammer gets two), and you'll want a pile of bronze foils for your first heating coils. At &bMV&r it also bends double plates.

And yes, it bends plates one for one too, if you'd rather keep it all electric.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Lathe
quests.subtitle: Get rid of your archaic tech
desc:
The Lathe is an important machine to help shape metals. It turns &6one Bolt into one Screw&r, where crafting by hand takes two bolts per screw.

It also turns an ingot into a rod plus two small piles of dust, which you can smelt back, so nothing is lost.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Polarizer
quests.subtitle: The Polarizer polarizes!
desc: One of the cheapest - if not the cheapest - &7LV&r machine. Use this to make &6Redstone-free Magnetic Rods&r for your Motors. Whenever you start to batch your Motors, this machine will save you stacks and stacks of Redstone.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Chemical Bath
quests.subtitle: The Chemical Bath bathes...
desc:
&lOutside of Ore Processing:&r

The Chemical Bath soaks items in fluids: planks in creosote become treated wood, wood pulp in water becomes paper, and it can dye and bleach various items and blocks.
{@pagebreak}

&lFor Ore Processing:&r

Some &aCrushed Ores&r have alternate routes to &aPurified Ore&r: a bath in &aMercury&r or &aSodium Persulfate&r. This step isn't really important, unless you really want that special &6Byproduct&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Programmed Circuits
quests.subtitle: Don't want to spend your circuits to select recipes?
desc:
By clicking the &6Circuit Configuration Slot&r in machines, you can create a &bghost Programmed Circuit&r. 

This is a fake circuit that allows you to select a given configuration for recipes! There's no need to spend your circuits crafting &bProgrammed Circuits&r anymore.

&dElectric Machines&r and &dItem Input Buses&r will have a Ghost Circuit Slot.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o This feature is originally from GTNH.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Canner
quests.subtitle: This machine does nothing exciting
desc: Make this machine when you feel like it's time you invested into Batteries.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Batteries!
quests.subtitle: Batteries for storing energy!
desc:
&aBatteries&r can be put into the energy slot at the bottom middle of machine GUIs, or in a &3Battery Buffer&r.

When inside your inventory, they can be sneak-right-clicked to allow the batteries to &dcharge&r your EU items.

&7LV&r, &bMV&r, and &6HV&r Batteries come in three forms: &dLithium&r has the best capacity, followed by &dCadmium&r, then &dSodium&r. A Canner fills a Battery Hull with two dusts.

In this pack &dSodium&r is the easy one: electrolyze &asalt&r from TFC halite. &dCadmium&r comes from bathing crushed tetrahedrite in sodium persulfate, and &dLithium&r waits for &bMV&r.

Get &eany&r &aBattery&r to complete this quest.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Battery Buffer
quests.subtitle: Useful if you don't want to build tons of generators
desc:
By itself, the Battery Buffer does nothing. However, if you place batteries inside its internal storage, it will act as a power buffer.

The &3Battery Buffer&r handles &9two Amps in&r, and &9one Amp out&r, &dper Battery&r. The output side has the dot, and all other sides are used as inputs.

&6It also charges electric tools placed inside it.&r

This is a must have if you don't have unlimited power at hand. Get &eany&r &7LV&r Battery Buffer to finish the quest. However, the 16 slots variant is likely overkill at this stage.
{@pagebreak}

&9Note:&r Don't loop your lossy Cables back to your Battery Buffer! If you think about it, you'll just end up voiding energy.

&l&3Lore:&r&o To be frank with you, the GTCE Battery Buffer was... mediocre. It's been reworked in GTCEu to provide a mix between GT5 and GTCE's functionality. Energy now splits evenly across all batteries!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: But wait, there's more!
quests.subtitle: You can't escape Greg...
desc:
We won't go over the &dfull scale of regular Ore Processing&r. Why regular? Some ores require special treatment, but that's a topic for much later. Oh no, we're already getting carried away!

Some machines like the &bChemical Bath&r or the &bElectrolyser&r could be useful.

Intimidated by ore processing? Check the dedicated &cOre Processing&r chapter for a full walkthrough!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Fluid Solidifier
quests.subtitle: The Fluid Solidifier solidifies...
desc:
Build this machine next to your &3Chemical Reactor&r to automatically solidify Rubber into &aRubber Sheets&r.

You can make your Chemical Reactor auto-output if you &dwrench&r the side of your &3Chemical Reactor&r and enable Fluid &9auto-output&r.

There will be more Fluids to solidify, so you may re-purpose your &3Fluid Solidifier&r when not crafting Rubber - or make a second one!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Cupronickel Coils
quests.subtitle: Baby's first heating coil
desc:
Your first Electric Blast Furnace needs &a16 Cupronickel Coils&r. Each is assembled from 8 Cupronickel Double Wires, 8 Bronze Foils and 144 mB of molten Tin Alloy, so the set takes &a128 Cupronickel&r ingots, &a128 Bronze Foils&r and &a16 Tin Alloy&r ingots' worth of metal.

You will also need Invar for the Heat Proof Casings, so get mining.

The Cupronickel Coils will allow the EBF to perform recipes up to &d1,800K&r (ignoring Voltage bonuses). That's pretty hot if you ask us.

&6Coils are explained further in the GregTech Power chapter (Blast Overclocking).&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Gas Collector
quests.subtitle: It'll take your breath away
desc:
The Gas Collector collects Air that can then be centrifuged into &aOxygen&r and &aNitrogen&r.

&l&3Lore:&r&o GregTech 5 players remember when they had to use a Compressor with IC2 cells to get Compressed Air... here, cell chemistry is no more.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Chemical Reactor
quests.subtitle: Chemistry for dummies
desc:
The &3Chemical Reactor&r will be required for &la lot&r of recipes.

Let's give it a spin: it makes &6Rubber three times cheaper&r than the alloy smelter. 9 raw rubber and 1 sulfur give 1296 mB of molten Rubber, nine ingots' worth, where the alloy smelter takes 3 raw rubber per ingot. Molten Rubber has to go into another machine, though.
{@pagebreak}

Here are some &aother machines&r you might want to aim for:

A &3Fluid Solidifier&r is useful to solidify your Rubber directly into &aRubber Sheets&r. You'll want these moving forward.

You could then make use of an &3Assembler&r to use your molten Rubber for &aCables&r. This isn't important for Tin Cables, but better cables will &eneed&r to be made in the Assembler.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Better bucket
quests.subtitle: You can see inside, unlike those drums...
desc:
Cells are an alternative form of Fluid storage. All Cell types with the same type and amount of Fluid inside them &6stack&r. They can be automatically filled with a &3Canning Machine&r.

The basic Fluid Cells hold &done bucket&r of Fluid, while the Steel Cells hold eight buckets.

Not sold on them yet? Unlike drums and buckets, cells &asafely contain&r their contents, preventing you from getting burnt, frozen, or floating. They're also significantly cheaper!
{@pagebreak}

Universal Cells hold up to &done bucket&r, but also can store &9fractions&r of Buckets. They're particularly ideal if you want to store leftover Fluid without crafting a whole Drum. 

Cells made from higher tier materials can hold even more fluid, but &9Drums&r and &9Super Tanks&r can hold even more.

Like Drums, Cells can be placed into a crafting grid to clear their contents.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Combo!
quests.subtitle: Time to end the misery of hand crafting rotors!
desc:
Use both of your new machines to turn a material into a Fluid, and solidify it back into a Rotor! That's &6four Ingots per Rotor&r, with no plates, ring or screw to make first.

You can do the same for &6Gears&r and &6Small Gears&r with their casting molds.

&9Note:&r Some metals require higher voltages than &7LV&r for Fluid Extraction, so make sure to keep an eye on the recipe tier in EMI.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Soldering Alloy
quests.subtitle: I got soul but I'm not a solder
desc:
&aSoldering Alloy&r is used solely as a &9Fluid&r, and in circuit recipes it's a &dcheaper&r stand-in for molten Tin: half as much per circuit.

The choice is yours. Save more materials? Make Soldering Alloy. Spend less time crafting materials? Tin is the way to go.

Mix 6 tin, 3 lead and 1 antimony dust in a Mixer, then melt the dust in an Extractor. Ignore the Alloy Blast Smelter recipes in EMI!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Electrolyzer
quests.subtitle: It goes bzzz
desc:
&lOutside of Ore Processing:&r

Similar to the Centrifuge, this machine does a lot of things - we can't hope to list them all! Fortunately, it's one of the cheapest &7LV&r machines, so grab it as soon as it becomes necessary.
{@pagebreak}

&lFor Ore Processing:&r

Okay, we lied. It's not &oexactly&r used for Ore Processing, it's actually used in the &adecomposition of Dusts&r. However, most of the useful electrolysis recipes are locked at &bMV&r. You can peep at the &emolecular formula&r in a dust's tooltip to see what you can get from electrolysis.
{@pagebreak}

&cTake caution!&r Due to how ores work, directly smelting dusts into Ingots can give higher metal yields than electrolysis. However, it means you lose the other products in the dust. You will have to decide whether you want to prioritise direct value, or byproduct count.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Cutter
quests.subtitle: The Cutter... cuts...
desc:
For now, you should use &9Water&r for its recipes instead of trying to acquire Lubricant.

If you don't have one yet, this machine will also cut &6Rods into four Bolts&r.

This machine is the only way to obtain &dGem Plates&r, which are needed to craft Filters, and by extension, the &3Gas Collector&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Centrifuge
quests.subtitle: It does the opposite of the Mixer
desc:
&lOutside of Ore Processing:&r

Oh boy, what can't this machine do? Decomposition recipes to separate dust types, separating air, do your taxes, and many others...

The list is too long! Let's just say &cyou need the Centrifuge&r.
{@pagebreak}

&lFor Ore Processing:&r

This takes &aImpure Dust&r or &aPurified Dust&r and turns them into clean Dust, plus an added tiny Dust &6Byproduct&r. This is outside of the optimal chain for Byproducts, but this is also the cheapest Ore Processing machine of the presented array to run and to setup on a small scale.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Spray Can
quests.subtitle: Time for server tag wars
desc:
Unfortunately, this is only an &lEmpty&r Spray Can, which you have to fill with Dye before using.

Any (or almost any) GregTech tile entity (machine, pipe, cable...) can be &6painted&r to one of the 16 colors of your choosing. This is great for screenshots, or to separate different setups for convenience in a Multiplayer base. They also help with distinguishing between pipelines and cables.

Holding the &aSpray Can&r in the offhand will automatically paint any block you place.

While this may not be immediately useful in &6LV&r, you can also paint Input and Output Buses and Hatches in matching colors to effectively "group" them together, ensuring recipe ingredients are kept separated if you're trying to use a single multiblock to do multiple recipes.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Liquid Extraction
quests.subtitle: The Extractor extracts...
desc:
Hm... didn't we make this joke already?

The &3Basic Extractor&r is your go-to machine for turning solids into liquids. Use it to melt Rubber that you previously solidified, to &dmelt Soldering Alloy&r for your circuits, and to &dmelt Red Alloy&r for the &6best Vacuum Tube recipe&r in the &3Assembler&r!
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o Did you notice this machine doubles as both an Extractor and a Fluid Extractor? The two of them were separate machines in previous versions of GregTech.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: The Circuit Assembler
quests.subtitle: Hopefully, your first MV Circuit expense
desc:
From now on, all Circuits should be made in a &3Circuit Assembler&r. Use it now to enjoy &6far cheaper LV and MV circuits&r.

Each time you upgrade to a new tier of &3Circuit Assembler&r, you will be able to craft more &dadvanced themes&r of circuit. These will use &ccomplex&r and &msometimes&r unfamiliar ingredients, but will be more efficient to craft overall.
{@pagebreak}

&l&3Lore:&r&o The Circuit Assembler has made appearances in and out of GregTech versions. GT5 did not have it, and it was reimplemented in GT5 Unofficial. GTCE decided not to port it, and the tug-of-war continues with its inclusion in GTCEu.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: The Arc Furnace
quests.subtitle: The Arc Furnace has never been so good
desc:
The &3Arc Furnace&r uses a lil' bit of &9Oxygen&r to smelt items in a different fashion than Furnaces.

It can &adouble your Glass&r (two per sand), gives you &aAnnealed Copper&r for cheaper electronic components, and melts metal parts such as plates, rods, wires and pipes back into ingots.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Breath of Fresh Oxygen
quests.subtitle: Achtually, it's Dioxygen...
desc:
You could waste &o&eprecious years of your life&r in EMI looking for the most optimal Oxygen recipe, given the many ways to obtain it. Various minerals will produce it when electrolyzed.

If only the quest book had more information!
{@pagebreak}

Surprise! The best source according to us (!) is &acentrifuging Air&r after making a &dGas Collector&r, which you might not be able to make just yet. This recipe also gives &aNitrogen&r, which is handy as it can speed up certain &3Electric Blast Furnace&r recipes.

The second best source according to us (!) is &aelectrolyzing Silicon Dioxide&r, which also gives you silicon. EMI shows where to get Silicon Dioxide.
{@pagebreak}

The third best source according to us (!) is &aelectrolyzing Water&r. It's slow and costly, so it suits &1Hydrogen&r production better. &4Don't use this method as your main source of Oxygen&r.

The fourth best source according to us (!) is &ato not void&r it, EVER! Any Oxygen obtained from any source is worth something and should be stored in Tanks.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Glued
quests.subtitle: What a sticky situation
desc:
You can now &3centrifuge&r &aSticky Resin&r, which will give you &aGlue&r in fluid form, plus raw rubber and the occasional Plantball.

Give yourself a headstart and get on producing Glue. You can use it to make &6cheaper Resistors&r, as well as &6cheaper Circuit Boards&r in the &3Assembler&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Gallium Arsenide
quests.subtitle: I hate byproducts, they're awesome
desc:
Many materials going forward cannot be smelted directly from any Ores! They are instead obtained as byproducts from processing of other ores. Gallium and Arsenic are &4among&r these materials.

For &dGallium&r, from worst to best:

&9- &3Electrolyze &aSphalerite&r dust for a low chance of it. Note that you lose out on direct smelting value.

&9-&r Process TFC &aSphalerite&r: macerating purified sphalerite ore, or running the crushed ore through a &3Thermal Centrifuge&r, gives it as a &6Byproduct&r.

For &dArsenic&r: TFC &aTetrahedrite&r carries &aRealgar&r. Run crushed tetrahedrite through a &3Thermal Centrifuge&r (or centrifuge pure tetrahedrite dust) for realgar dust, then &3Centrifuge&r the realgar into arsenic and sulfur.

Mix one gallium and one arsenic dust for two Gallium Arsenide.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Phenolic Printed Circuit Board
quests.subtitle: They don't make 'em like this any more...
desc:
This Circuit Board is used to create &dMV Circuits&r!

First make a Phenolic Circuit Board in the &3Assembler&r from wood pulp and &aGlue&r. Then etch it: by hand with 8 silver wires, or in the &3Chemical Reactor&r with 4 silver foils and &aIron III Chloride&r or &aSodium Persulfate&r, which takes &6only a quarter of the Silver&r.

Given how painful those chemicals may be to obtain &oright now&r, you can simply use more silver from TFC's native silver.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o Back in GTCEu 1.12.2, these circuit boards were called &2Good Circuit Boards&f. Not exactly a fitting name, as they're &4rather evil&f to craft.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Diode
quests.subtitle: Don't be swayed by EMI!
desc:
Don't let EMI fool you... at &7LV&r only two of its recipes work: the liquid glass ones, with fine copper (or annealed copper) wire and a small pile of Gallium Arsenide.

Diodes have an infamously &4nasty recipe&r, but they will become cheaper and more convenient once you can obtain &ePolyethylene&r.

This is required for &dMV Circuits&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: First MV Circuit!
quests.subtitle: Does that mean we're at MV yet?
desc:
Well... got any Aluminium Ingots yet?

Each Electric Age has Circuits corresponding to its tier. The Good Electronic Circuit is the &dfirst MV Circuit&r you can make: a Phenolic Printed Circuit Board, Basic Electronic Circuits, Diodes and copper wire.

Always be on the lookout for a cheaper way to make your circuits - new sets of recipes become available each time you make a new tier of &2Circuit Assembler&r. Conveniently, this circuit unlocks the first one.

&6Having this and Aluminium will grant access to MV Machines.&r
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Aluminium Dust
quests.subtitle: Time for an adventure
desc:
There's many minerals that can be electrolyzed into aluminium, but most of them are off-limits until &bMV&r. TFC's gems are the exception: electrolyze &aSapphire&r dust in an &7LV&r Electrolyzer, or blast &aRuby&r straight into aluminium nuggets in the EBF. Several ore processing chains also give aluminium dust as a byproduct. TFC's field guide tells you where to find sapphire and ruby.

Once you have enough aluminium, we recommend making the Electrolyzer your first &bMV&r machine to unlock all the other options.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Multiblock Techniques
quests.subtitle: Oh we love multiblocks right?
desc:
This is the &6basics&r of what you need to build your first &bEBF&r, though it is highly customisable. Remember to use &6EMI&r, use &6U&r on the controller and don't hesitate to &6left click on the structure blocks&r to see what the possibilities are.

An important notice, each Energy Hatch can accept &a2A&r, which means that at &7LV&r they can each handle &a64 EU/t&r. With two of them, your &eEBF&r can run at &a128 EU/t&r.

For more details about this mechanic, refer to the &eGregTech Power&r chapter, specifically the &eSpending Energy&r quest.

Multiblocks bear a large variety of interesting mechanics that might seem daunting, but don't worry - you don't need to do anything fancy right yet. You'll learn more as you go!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Turbo Charger
quests.subtitle: Useful to charge your electric tools faster
desc:
&oThis quest's subject is optional, but may still be of interest to you. We've put it here in the name of completeness.&r

The &3Turbo Charger&r charges electric items such as &9Drills&r extremely quickly.

It accepts up to 4 Amps for every item it charges, making it &6twice as fast&r as the &3Battery Buffer&r. It cannot discharge, though.

&eAny&r Charger will complete this Quest.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Mixer
quests.subtitle: The Mixer mixes...
desc:
The Mixer is the GregTech way of alloying: &amix dusts together&r, then smelt them into ingots or melt them into fluids. Any new alloy goes through it, and the old ones can too.

It also &6speeds up&r TFC's colored steels: &aBlack Steel&r, &aRed Steel&r and &aBlue Steel&r dust come straight out of it, ready for the EBF. Even if you don't think you need it now, you'll find it &6essential&r later on.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Nitrogen Gas
quests.subtitle: Your EBF booster
desc: For now, your only use for Nitrogen will be to make your EBF &6faster&r, which may not sound like that big of a deal, but with how much you'll be using it, it's definitely worth setting up. Faster recipes mean less energy used too!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Casting Mold and Rubber Sheets
quests.subtitle: Even cheaper rubber
desc:
You're gonna need a lot of &6Rubber Sheets&r, and later on other plastics too.

With the Chemical Reactor's cheaper molten Rubber, the &3Fluid Solidifier&r and a Plate Casting Mold cast it straight into sheets: 144 mB each, no rubber ingots or press in between.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Your next machines
quests.subtitle: More options!
desc:
Now that you've got some electricity going, it's time to use it! We recommend starting by making machines that will make it easier and cheaper to make even more machines.

Create already does part of that job in this pack: the press makes plates one for one and the saw slits a plate into two wires. GregTech's machines add what Create can't: foils, screws, fine wire, magnetic rods, molten metals and chemistry.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: The Combustion Generator
quests.subtitle: It does boom and make energy
desc:
The &7LV Combustion Generator&r burns liquid fuels that carry a lot of energy per mB, so a drum of fuel can power a generator far from your base.

Like other &7LV Generators&r, it produces &a32 EU/t&r.

In this pack its fuels (ethanol, methanol, &2Bio Diesel&r, then oil products) arrive at &bMV&r, so this one can wait until then.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Explain energy to me
quests.subtitle: There is a whole chapter about energy
desc:
GregTech's energy system (EU, Energy Units) works differently to FE (Forge Energy), the system used by almost every other mod, so the book has a whole chapter on it: &eGregTech Power&r.

It might look like a lot of reading, but it's important to understand if you want to avoid accidents and get the most out of your power generation.

In this pack, &7LV&r power comes from Steam Turbines fed by your boilers. Gas Turbines can burn methane, and Combustion Generators get their fuels at &bMV&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Cupronickel Ingots
quests.subtitle: It's an alloy
desc:
A big part of progression in GregTech revolves around gaining access to new materials that you'll use to upgrade your machines or unlock advanced components.

One such material you'll encounter is &bCupronickel&r — the beginning of a long journey.
This material is used to build your first &6Electric Blast Furnace&r, an essential step in your industrial growth.

Luckily, this first step is fairly simple: an Alloy Smelter turns one copper and one nickel (from TFC garnierite) into two cupronickel. So even if the coils ask for &b128 Cupronickel&r, don't worry — it's easier than it looks!&r

Later on, their counterparts will become much more complex, so enjoy the simplicity while it lasts!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: The Gas Turbine
quests.subtitle: For petrochemical enthusiasts
desc:
The &cGas Turbine&r works exactly like the other &6generators&r, but burns gases.

At &7LV&r that means &7Methane&r: a Centrifuge gets 60 mB from every rubber log, along with sticky resin you need anyway. It won't power a factory alone, but a rubber tree farm keeps it going.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Lost?
quests.subtitle: This is all very overwhelming
desc:
Getting into &7LV&r opens up a LOT of options, so it's easy to get lost. Here's our recommendations:

1) Set up a source of power: Steam Turbines fed by your boilers. Don't cheap out, build multiple generators!

Be sure to &eread the GregTech Power chapter&r so you get a good understanding of how EU, Volts, Amps, and Cable Loss all work.
{@pagebreak}

2) Focus on machines that make building more machines cheaper.

The Polarizer is a super cheap machine that can magnetize rods for basically free. Create's press and saw already make plates and wires; add a Bender for foils, a Lathe for screws and a Cutter for bolts.

After that, focus on making Rubber cheaper with a Chemical Reactor and Fluid Solidifier, and making electronic components cheaper with an Assembler.

Once everything's at its cheapest, make sure you craft components in batches to save you lots of time.
{@pagebreak}

3) Build a Canner and make some batteries. Battery Buffers will help a lot with the growth of your factory.

4) &7LV&r has two main end goals, the &aCircuit Assembler&r and the &aElectric Blast Furnace&r. You should now be ready to tackle those.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Even more machines
quests.subtitle: Now the fun begins
desc:
Now that you've got a few machines going, it's time to put them to work.

The Assembler will make electronic components cheaper, while the Chemical Reactor, Extractor, and Fluid Solidifier will make Rubber cheaper. After that, the rest of &7LV&r is yours to explore!
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Basic Distillery
quests.subtitle: The distillery distills...
desc:
The Distillery is kind of like a centrifuge, but mostly for organic/petrochemical fluids: one input, one chosen output, picked with a Programmed Circuit. This will change once you get the Distillation Tower.

At &7LV&r its handiest job is turning &7Creosote&r from your coke ovens into &eLubricant&r, which the Cutter and other machines can use. Most of its other recipes, such as phenol and toluene from wood tar, need &bMV&r.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter low_voltage

quests.title: Let's do some explaining
quests.subtitle: It's not as bad as you think
desc:
We know that GregTech isn’t the easiest mod to get into — especially when it comes to the &cenergy system&r. That’s why we’ll take our time in this chapter to explain as much as we can.

Some things here might not make full sense until later in your progression, so don’t stress yourself. Just try to understand what you can for now, and feel free to &dcome back to this chapter&r whenever you have questions.

We’ve split this chapter into &efour categories&r, each one covering a topic related to the GregTech Energy System. We’ll provide as many examples as possible to help you understand how it all works.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Moving your Energy
quests.subtitle: So, energy transfer, huh
desc:
Moving Energy in GregTech means understanding a few core mechanics.

First, &bEnergy Tiers&r. From &aLV&r to &cUHV&r, everything in GregTech — wires, machines, recipes — is tied to a tier. You’ll need the &ecorrect cable material&r to move energy. For example:
&7•&r Tin wire = &aLV&r
&7•&r Copper wire = &bMV&r

Second, you’ve got the &bAmperage&r mechanic. Think of 1 Amp (or 1A) as &ea packet of energy&r. Machines request energy "packets", which then get sent down the wire.
&7•&r 1A of LV = &a32 EU&r
&7•&r 1A of HV = &e512 EU&r

Most machines and energy hatches will only request &62A at maximum&r.

Mastering these two ideas is key before going further into energy distribution.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Storing Energy
quests.subtitle: Gotta put all that juice somewhere
desc:
Storing your energy is one of the most fundamental pillars of the power system in GregTech.

Why is that? Simply because even the strongest generators won't keep up when you start a big craft.

GregTech provides several ways to store large amounts of EU. These storages act as a buffer between your energy production and the machines that drain it during long operations.

Whether you're running an Electric Blast Furnace or a whole HV-EV crafting chain, you'll want that backup of energy to keep everything stable.

Don't underestimate the power of a good battery — it may just be the thing that saves your base from a blackout during critical moments.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Producing Energy
quests.subtitle: Gas or Oil?
desc:
It's all about making energy, right? This part won't be the most complicated one: in this pack all electricity comes from &5GregTech's&r own generators. Steam turbines fed by your boilers come first; gas turbines and combustion generators join them as you unlock their fuels.

You'll learn about the various &6methods to generate energy&r, as well as some of the &afuels&r you can use to get the most out of your setup.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Spending Energy
quests.subtitle: Oh you will spend energy
desc:
How to spend all this energy?

Use your machines! Sounds simple, right?
Well... not exactly. There are many small details worth learning.

Basic Machines:
- These machines are simple.
- They can request up to &a2A&r each.
- If you input a higher tier of energy... &4💥 they explode&r.

GregTech Multiblocks:
Now things get interesting. Multiblocks offer more flexibility and power — &eif&r you understand how they work.
{@pagebreak}

Standard Mechanics:
- If a multiblock can accept two Energy Hatches (most of them), this allows you to use higher-tier recipes than the machine's base tier.

Example:
If you're building an Electric Blast Furnace and you install two &7LV&r Energy Hatches, it will be able to process &bMV&r-tier EBF recipes.

This is one of the key benefits of multiblocks over single-block machines — to upgrade them to the next tier, you only have to swap out their energy hatches instead of replacing the whole machine.
{@pagebreak}

Some multiblocks only accept one Energy Hatch, but that doesn't limit them to 2 amps! From &5EV&r on there are 4A and 16A Energy Hatches.

More amps on a single hatch let the machine &bOverclock&r recipes, but not run higher-tier recipes. That limitation is intentional, to keep multiblocks from skipping GregTech's tier progression.

So remember: More amps on a single hatch means faster processing, but two hatches are required to unlock higher-tier recipes.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Moving with wires
quests.subtitle: Funky to place
desc:
Moving energy around in GregTech can be tricky — &bcables lose energy&r. For every block, for every amp, some EU is lost along the way. But don't worry, there are solutions:

&7•&r Cover your wires with rubber. Cables (insulated wires) lose less than bare wires, and they won't shock you. Just check the quest items for a reference.

&7•&r Pick the right material. Hover over a wire or cable to see its maximum voltage, maximum amperage and loss per block; better materials lose less for the energy they carry.

&7•&r &bSuperconductors&r. These beauties are a bit pricier, but they have &9zero loss&r. They don't need rubber covers, and won't zap you either. Just be aware that they're usually only craftable near the end of their tier.

Optimize your energy flow — &breduce losses&r and make your systems more efficient.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Managing Amp
quests.subtitle: It burns?
desc:
You’ll notice each wire has its own &eMax Amperage&r — that’s the amount of amps a cable can safely carry before burning.
To know how many amps will flow through a cable, you must consider two things:

- A Generator or Battery outputs a specific amount of Amps:
Battery Buffers will output as many amps as they have batteries inside.
Every single-block generator outputs &e1A&r.
For multiblock generators, it depends on the &aDynamo Energy Hatch&r — the value is shown in its tooltip.

Amperage output is also based on what is needed: each machine connected to a power line will request amps to fill its internal buffer.
{@pagebreak}

Let’s look at an example:
You have &e6 machines&r connected to an &e8x Battery Buffer&r filled with 8 batteries.
The buffer will try to send &e1A&r to each machine — that’s &e6A&r total.
The amps are delivered in order: the closest machines get power first, and the furthest ones last.
If your cables only support &c4A&r, they’ll &cBURN&r. You’ll need &a8A cables&r in this case.

&bTip:&r The first machine in the line might need a cable that handles &e8A&r,
but the last machine may only need &e1A&r, as it’s only receiving what’s left.
&c⚠ Be careful:&r adding another machine at the end could cause the cable to burn if it exceeds the limit.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Battery Buffer
quests.subtitle: The basic battery buffer beckons batteries
desc:
Battery Buffers are your basic machines to store and manage energy — though technically, they don't store energy on their own. They simply serve as a housing for your batteries.

&c⚠ If you don't want them to explode&r:
- &4Never input higher-tier energy&r into a lower-tier Battery Buffer.
- Batteries can only be charged if they are of &cequal or lower tier&r than the Battery Buffer.
{@pagebreak}

A Battery Buffer takes in up to two amps and puts out one amp for each battery inside.
So a full 4x Battery Buffer can take in &a8A&r — but will only output &e4A&r max.

&eReminder&r:
- No batteries = no output.
- The number of batteries sets the number of Amps it outputs. (That means a &68x Battery Buffer&r with only &e3 batteries&r will only output &e3A&r.)

Use them wisely — they are the foundation of any stable energy network.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Storing Fuel
quests.subtitle: There's more kinds of batteries than just electric ones
desc:
Obviously, storing energy can also mean storing the fuel that makes it.

For this, Drums and Crates are decent early options, but don't overlook GregTech's &dSuper Tanks&r and &dSuper Chests&r.
{@pagebreak}

These hold huge amounts of fluid or items — handy for fuelling generators far from your main base without building a whole cable network.

Load them up with fuel and let them handle the rest. With proper planning, an outpost can run with no live connection to your central grid.

Energy doesn't always come in wires — sometimes, it comes in barrels.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Super Batteries
quests.subtitle: Sci-Fi power storage
desc:
In &7LV&r and &bMV&r, you probably built your first batteries from Sodium or Cadmium.

But let's be real — these are the weakest batteries GregTech has to offer.

Here are the stronger alternatives: the &acrystal batteries&r. The &aEnergium Crystal&r grows in an &6HV&r Autoclave, the &aLapotron Crystal&r is put together in an &5EV&r Assembler. They store way more energy and can help you push your factory to the next tier.

Are they more expensive? Of course. But let's be real...
Power is Power. Who's counting?
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: The Large Steam Turbine
quests.subtitle: Your boilers, scaled up
desc:
The &6Large Steam Turbine&r — or &dLST&r — is GregTech's first large generator, built at &6HV&r from an HV hull, HV circuits, steel gears and large steel pipes. In a pack that runs on boilers, it's the natural next step after a wall of single-block steam turbines.

To make it work you'll need an Input Hatch for steam, an Output Hatch for the distilled water it gives back, and a Maintenance Hatch. Like all Large Turbines, it takes a Rotor Holder on one side and a Dynamo Hatch to extract the power.
{@pagebreak}

The Rotor Holder must be at least &6HV&r, and each tier above that doubles the output. The rotor's power multiplies it further, and its efficiency stretches each mB of steam.

Size the Dynamo Hatch to what your holder and rotor produce: a normal Dynamo Hatch handles 2A. Check EMI's multiblock preview for the exact structure.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: The Large Gas Turbine
quests.subtitle: The big gas burner
desc:
The &6Large Gas Turbine&r — also known as &dLGT&r — is the large generator for gas fuels. You can build your first one at &5EV&r from an EV hull, EV circuits, stainless steel gears and large stainless steel pipes.

Like the other large turbines it needs a Maintenance Hatch, an Input Hatch for the gas, a Rotor Holder and a Dynamo Hatch. It also needs a Muffler Hatch, but no Output Hatch.
{@pagebreak}

Its output doubles with every Rotor Holder tier above &5EV&r, and the rotor's power multiplies it further. Size the Dynamo Hatch to match: a normal one handles 2A, so a strong turbine may need a 4A hatch.

The Efficiency stat of a Turbine Rotor makes each mB of fuel last longer.

Turbines burn fuel while they run, so switch them off when your batteries are full, for example with an Energy Detector cover and a Machine Controller cover.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: The Blast Overclocking
quests.subtitle: You don't need to understand this one
desc:
If you haven't learnt about Perfect Overclocking yet, read the Overclock quest first.

The &3Electric Blast Furnace&r has a special ability: it can &ePerfect Overclock&r recipes depending on the &ctemperature of the machine&r. You can check its current temperature by clicking on the controller.

There are two ways to increase the temperature:
1) Upgrade the coils
2) Use higher-tier energy: every tier above &bMV&r adds 100K
{@pagebreak}

To see the temperature of a coil, hover over it.

Once you know your machine's temperature, you'll need the temperature of the recipe. The easiest way to find it is to use EMI.

With both values, you can do a quick calculation to see if Perfect Overclocking applies:
&bYour machine must be at least 1800K hotter than the recipe for each overclock you want to be perfect.&r

It also gets a small energy discount for every 900K it runs above the recipe.
{@pagebreak}

Example:
- Stainless Steel requires &c1700K&r and is an &6HV&r recipe.
- You run it on &5EV&r power: that's one overclock.
- For it to be perfect, the furnace needs 1700 + 1800 = &c3500K&r.
- Cupronickel coils (1800K) reach 2000K on EV and Kanthal coils (2700K) 2900K: a normal overclock. Nichrome coils (3600K) reach 3800K: a perfect one.

Feeling overwhelmed? Just remember this: better coils = faster and cheaper recipes.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Overclock
quests.subtitle: Basic upgrade mechanic
desc:
Have you heard about Overclocking, but don't really understand what it is? Let's take some time to explain it.

We should start with the basics:
&dLV&r represents a maximum of 32 EU/t — sometimes less, but never more.
&dMV&r goes up to 128 EU/t.
&dHV&r reaches 512 EU/t.
Basically, every tier is a 4x increase in power usage.
{@pagebreak}

What happens when you run a lower-tier recipe in a higher-tier machine? That's what we call &eOverclocking&r!

An &dMV&r recipe (33–128 EU/t) run in an &dHV&r machine will both: 1) Use 4x more energy, and 2) Be 2x faster.

The same MV recipe in an &dEV&r machine? 16x the energy cost, but only 4x faster.

As you can see, it's more power efficient to use multiple machines rather than overclocking a single one.
But let's be real: in most setups, you'll prefer overclocking to building a ton of the same machines.

Still, it's good to know this early on, when energy is tight.
{@pagebreak}

There's a special kind of overclocking exclusive to just a few multiblocks: &ePerfect Overclocking&r.
Here, instead of 4x energy for 2x speed, you get &a4x energy&r for &a4x speed&r! This makes it just as efficient as running multiple machines.

The ones you'll meet:
- Large Chemical Reactor, always
- Electric Blast Furnace, when its coils run hot enough (see the Blast Overclocking quest)
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Subtick
quests.subtitle: Parallel?
desc:
Another hidden mechanic in GregTech Multiblocks: the &dSubtick&r.

What is it? Subtick kicks in when a recipe gets so fast it would take less than one tick. Normally, machines can't go faster than one recipe per tick — but with Subtick, they can!

How does it work? Once a recipe hits 1 tick, more power can't make it any shorter.
Instead of wasting that power, the machine &aruns several recipes in parallel internally&r.
{@pagebreak}
&dNote&r: the &6Large Chemical Reactor&r, an &6HV&r multiblock, combines Subtick with Perfect Overclocking, so extra power is never wasted on it. That makes it the best home for your fast chemistry.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: Gas Fuels
quests.subtitle: Everyone's favorite
desc:
All of these fuels are used in &2Gas Turbines&r — ranked here from the least efficient to the best: natural gas, methane, refinery gas, LPG, benzene and nitrobenzene.

Gas fuels hold less energy per mB than combustion fuels. That doesn't make them worse — you just need more millibuckets for the same output. Later, they can feed the &2Large Gas Turbine&r, a very powerful multiblock.
{@pagebreak}
At &7LV&r your gas is &eMethane&r: a Centrifuge gets 60 mB from every rubber log, along with sticky resin. The others come from oil processing at &bMV&r and later; check EMI for each one's chain.
quests.source: Ported from TerraFirmaGreg (LGPL-3.0), commit b43cb47849, chapter gregtech_energy

quests.title: This is Steam
quests.subtitle: Not much of a choice
desc:
Steam isn't complicated — just boil water.

To do it at scale, build GregTech's &6Large Boilers&r: Bronze first (LV circuits, tin cables and a Bronze Firebox Casing), then Steel, Titanium and Tungstensteel. Each tier makes a lot more steam. They burn solid fuels or liquids such as lava and creosote; EMI lists them all.

As a reminder: &e2 mB&r of steam = &e1 EU&r in a steam turbine.
